tldr: For the published global OVS staggered-DDD model, this note proves the full-data/observed-law image for arbitrary covariate support.  At fixed finite-support covariate laws it exhausts the observed tangent normal generated by every period-admissible clean cohort and derives the canonical gradient \(\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}=\psi_P^0-r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)'K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)^\dagger Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\).  Conditional loading by \(b^\star(X)\) remains only the optimum inside the aggregate pairwise-score family and is canonical exactly when its published-normal equation holds.  A fixed-support cross-fitted estimator attains \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\), and a finite-support moment map gives pointwise Wald inference for comparator efficiency gaps away from equality and rank changes.  In the corrected bounded binary witness, the best joint constant loading loses exactly \(3/512\) and the published componentwise OVS loading loses \(15/512\), both relative to the published bound.

project_justification.gap: Ortiz--Villavicencio and Sant'Anna establish staggered-DDD identification, pairwise-score limit theory, constant componentwise weighting, and a two-period DDD efficient influence function, while Akbari, Kiyavash, and Ghassami derive a nonparametric two-period panel-DDD efficient influence function.  These results do not provide the fixed-finite-support observed tangent exhaustion for the overidentified global staggered OVS restriction system or pointwise inference for the resulting published-bound comparator gap.
project_justification.niche: The global OVS model contains period-specific eligibility-gap normal directions beyond terminal clean-comparison contrasts.  At fixed finite-support covariate laws, an explicit affine-support right inverse and bounded likelihood tilts exhaust those directions.  The resulting canonical object is the projection of a reference gradient onto the published tangent space, including singular normal operators and shared-cell covariances; the conditional loading \(b^\star(X)\) solves a distinct restricted score-family problem.  Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie's Theorem 3.2 is used only as a conditional-precision architectural comparator, and no nesting relation is asserted.
project_justification.fill: The note proves the general observed-law/full-data equivalence, proves fixed-finite-support published tangent exhaustion by an exact dominated-tilt construction, derives the singular Moore--Penrose canonical projection, and gives an attaining fixed-support cross-fitted estimator.  It also supplies an exact two-period panel-DDD reduction, a finite-moment map with pointwise Wald inference for the published-bound comparator gap, and a corrected bounded witness whose best joint constant and componentwise OVS losses are \(3/512\) and \(15/512\), respectively.

related_work: Ortiz--Villavicencio and Sant'Anna provide the staggered-DDD identifying architecture, pairwise-score limit theory, constant componentwise benchmark, and, in Supplemental Appendix Lemma A.2, a two-period panel-DDD efficient influence function.  Akbari, Kiyavash, and Ghassami's Theorem 5 gives the corresponding nonparametric four-cell panel-DDD efficient influence function; Proposition \(\ref{prop:two-period-eif-reduction}\) gives the note's term-by-term singleton-comparison reduction, including the target-share derivative.  Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie's Theorem 3.2 supplies a normalized conditional-precision efficient influence-function formula for its staggered-DiD target; it is retained only as an architectural comparator, and no equivalence or nesting of tangent spaces is claimed.  Newey supplies the cited generalized-inverse conditional-moment geometry, Chernozhukov and coauthors supply the cross-fitting template used by the attainment result, Hsieh supplies the shared-comparison fixed-weight limit-law comparator, and Borusyak, Jaravel, and Spiess delimit the distinct efficient-imputation route.  The contribution here is general observable/full-data equivalence together with fixed-finite-support OVS tangent exhaustion, canonical projection, attainment, and pointwise comparator-gap inference.
technical_internal_limitation: The observed-law/full-data equivalence allows arbitrary covariate support, but tangent exhaustion and canonicality are proved only at conditional-mean interior laws with fixed finite covariate support.  The proof uses a finite collection of affine-support right inverses; no measurable uniformly bounded analogue is established for continuously distributed covariates.  Target attainment and comparator-gap inference are likewise fixed-support and pointwise.  Gap inference assumes positive influence variance and separation from equality by \(\delta_0>0\) and is not uniform across comparator or normal-rank changes.  The external efficient-influence-function equivalence is confined to the two-period, two-cohort, singleton-comparison panel-DDD specialization.  No nesting with the distinct staggered-DiD tangent system, growing-sieve continuous-covariate theorem, or uniform confidence procedure under weak or changing positive eigenvalues of \(K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)\) is proved.
honest_scope: The note covers a fixed finite horizon and target set.  Its observable/full-data characterization is general in the covariate distribution, whereas its tangent-space, canonical-gradient, attainment, and comparator-gap inference results require fixed finite covariate support and are pointwise at conditional-mean interior laws.  It distinguishes the published bound \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\), the localized bound \(V_{\mathrm{can}}\), and the aggregate score-family variance \(V_{\mathrm{agg}}\); \(b^\star(X)'\Psi_P\) is not presented as canonical without its published-normal equation.  In the bounded witness, all normal closures coincide, so \(3/512\) is the minimum published-bound loss over deterministic feasible loadings and \(15/512\) is the componentwise OVS loss at \(r=\omega_2=1/2\).  The two-period influence-function comparison is an exact special-case reduction.  A CRAN \(\texttt{triplediff}\) backend is proposed only as future work.  No continuous-covariate canonicality or Wald theorem, equality-boundary inference, staggered-DiD tangent-space nesting, or rank-uniform guarantee is claimed.
interpretation: At a fixed finite-support covariate law there are three precision frontiers.  Conditional loading by \(b^\star(X)\) minimizes variance within the aggregate pairwise-score family.  Projection against \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\) gives the larger localized model's bound, while projection against the exhaustively justified \(Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\) gives the published model's canonical gradient and smaller bound.  A loaded pairwise score is therefore called semiparametrically efficient only when its published-normal conditional moment is zero.  The corrected witness makes the normal closures coincide but separates the comparators: the best deterministic loading loses \(3/512\) at the benchmark and the componentwise OVS rule loses \(15/512\).  Integration of the certified fixed-support estimator, diagnostics, and pointwise gap interval as an optional CRAN \(\texttt{triplediff}\) backend is future work, not an implemented contribution of this note.

definitions.name: Published global OVS staggered-DDD model
definitions.construction:
\(\mathcal M\) is the class of full-data laws \(Q\) satisfying consistency and no effect on ineligible units, global mean no anticipation for every finite \(a\in\mathcal G\) and every \(u<a\), and the following literal OVS-indexed condition: for every finite \(g\in\mathcal G\), every \(u\in\{g,\ldots,T\}\), and every \(c\in\mathcal C_u^{\mathrm{OVS}}=\{a\in\mathcal G:a>u\}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
&E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,1)\mid G=g,S=1,X]
-E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,0)\mid G=g,S=0,X]\\
&\qquad=
E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,1)\mid G=c,S=1,X]
-E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,0)\mid G=c,S=0,X]
\end{aligned}
\]
almost surely.  Thus \(\mathcal M\) is the published global OVS class, not the target-localized clean-through-terminal model.

definitions.name: Joint OVS score vector
definitions.construction:
For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\) and \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), let
\(e_{a,s,k}(O)=\sum_{u=g}^t\{\Delta Y_u-m_{a,s,u}(X)\}\), and retain the uncentered ratio pseudo-outcome
\[
R_{k,c,P}(O)=\frac{1}{\pi_{g,1}}\left[\mathbf 1_{g,1}\{q_{k,c}(X)+e_{g,1,k}(O)\}-\frac{p_{g,1}(X)}{p_{g,0}(X)}\mathbf 1_{g,0}e_{g,0,k}(O)-\frac{p_{g,1}(X)}{p_{c,1}(X)}\mathbf 1_{c,1}e_{c,1,k}(O)+\frac{p_{g,1}(X)}{p_{c,0}(X)}\mathbf 1_{c,0}e_{c,0,k}(O)\right].
\]
The centered ratio-functional score is
\[
\Psi_{k,c,P}(O)=R_{k,c,P}(O)-\frac{\theta_k(P)}{\pi_{g,1}}\mathbf 1_{g,1}
=\frac{1}{\pi_{g,1}}\left[\mathbf 1_{g,1}\{q_{k,c}(X)-\theta_k(P)+e_{g,1,k}(O)\}-\frac{p_{g,1}(X)}{p_{g,0}(X)}\mathbf 1_{g,0}e_{g,0,k}(O)-\frac{p_{g,1}(X)}{p_{c,1}(X)}\mathbf 1_{c,1}e_{c,1,k}(O)+\frac{p_{g,1}(X)}{p_{c,0}(X)}\mathbf 1_{c,0}e_{c,0,k}(O)\right].
\]
Stack both vectors in the fixed order \(\mathcal I\).  The extra target-cell term is the derivative of the denominator \(\pi_{g,1}\); in particular, the former formula \(\Psi=R-A\theta\) is not the gradient of the ratio functional when \(\pi_{g,1}\) varies.

definitions.name: Aggregate conditional projection loading
definitions.construction: For almost every \(x\), \(b^{\star}(x)\) is selected from \(\arg\min_{b\in\mathbb R^M:A'b=\omega}b'\Gamma(x)b\) by requiring \(N'\{b-b^0\}\in\operatorname{range}H(x)\).

definitions.name: Moore--Penrose aggregate, localized, and published diagnostics
definitions.construction:
For each training complement of \(I_\ell\), form \(\widehat\Omega^{-\ell}\).  For the OVS comparator, solve each block KKT system
\[
\begin{pmatrix}\widehat\Omega^{-\ell}_{kk}&\mathbf 1\\ \mathbf 1'&0\end{pmatrix}
\binom{v_k}{\lambda_k}=\binom{0}{\omega_k}
\]
by its Moore--Penrose inverse; for the joint constant comparator, solve
\[
\begin{pmatrix}\widehat\Omega^{-\ell}&A\\ A'&0\end{pmatrix}
\binom{v}{\lambda}=\binom{0}{\omega}
\]
in the same way.  Take the minimum-Euclidean-norm loading component \(\widehat b^{-\ell,\mathrm{cmp}}\).  Report the three conditional residuals
\[
\widehat d^{-\ell}_{\mathrm{cmp}}(x)
=N'\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x)\widehat b^{-\ell,\mathrm{cmp}},
\]
\[
\widehat e^{-\ell}_{\mathrm{cmp}}(x)
=\widehat E_{-\ell}\!\left[
\widehat Z^{\mathrm{per},-\ell}
\{\widehat b^{-\ell,\mathrm{cmp}\prime}\widehat\Psi^{-\ell}\}
\mid X=x\right],
\]
\[
\widehat f^{-\ell}_{\mathrm{cmp}}(x)
=\widehat E_{-\ell}\!\left[
\widehat Z^{\mathrm{OVS},-\ell}
\{\widehat b^{-\ell,\mathrm{cmp}\prime}\widehat\Psi^{-\ell}\}
\mid X=x\right].
\]
They diagnose, respectively, equality with the aggregate pairwise-score optimum, the localized-model bound, and the published OVS bound.  Stack them as
\(\widehat D^{-\ell}_{\mathrm{cmp}}=(\widehat d^{-\ell}_{\mathrm{cmp}},\widehat e^{-\ell}_{\mathrm{cmp}},\widehat f^{-\ell}_{\mathrm{cmp}})\).

definitions.name: Published OVS-complete efficient cross-fitted estimator
definitions.construction:
For each training complement of \(I_\ell\), estimate all globally OVS-retained propensities and one-step regressions by \(\widehat p^{-\ell}\) and \(\widehat m^{-\ell}\), clipped to the overlap interval, and form
\[
\widehat S_i^{\mathrm{OVS},-\ell}=S^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O_i;\widehat\eta^{-\ell}),
\qquad \widehat\eta^{-\ell}=(\widehat p^{-\ell},\widehat m^{-\ell}).
\]
Using training-cell averages, form
\[
\widehat K_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}(x)
=\widehat E_{-\ell}[\widehat S^{\mathrm{OVS},-\ell}
\widehat S^{\mathrm{OVS},-\ell\prime}\mid X=x],
\qquad
\widehat r_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}(x)
=\widehat E_{-\ell}[\widehat S^{\mathrm{OVS},-\ell}\widehat\psi^{0,-\ell}\mid X=x],
\]
where \(\widehat\psi^{0,-\ell}\) uses the denominator-corrected reference scores and training-sample preliminary ratios.  Retain eigenvalues of \(\widehat K_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}(x)\) exceeding \(\tau_n\), use the Moore--Penrose inverse of the retained part, and set
\[
\widehat\alpha_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}(x)
=\{\widehat K_{\mathrm{OVS},\tau}^{-\ell}(x)\}^{\dagger}
\widehat r_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}(x).
\]
For each target block, form the cross-fitted bracket numerator \(\widehat B_{i,k,c_0(k)}^{-\ell}\), but divide its final sample average by the global empirical share
\(\widehat\pi_{g,1}=n^{-1}\sum_i\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\}\).  Equivalently, write the resulting raw ratio pseudo-outcome as \(\widehat R_{i,k,c_0(k)}\).  Return
\[
\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}
=\frac1n\sum_{\ell=1}^L\sum_{i\in I_\ell}
\left\{\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\omega_k\widehat R_{i,k,c_0(k)}
-\widehat\alpha_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}(X_i)'
\widehat S_i^{\mathrm{OVS},-\ell}\right\}.
\]
Let \(\widehat\theta_k=n^{-1}\sum_i\widehat R_{i,k,c_0(k)}\).  For \(i\in I_\ell\), define
\[
\widehat\phi_i=
\sum_{k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K}\omega_k
\left\{\widehat R_{i,k,c_0(k)}
-\widehat\theta_k\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\}}{\widehat\pi_{g,1}}\right\}
-\widehat\alpha_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}(X_i)'
\widehat S_i^{\mathrm{OVS},-\ell},
\]
\[
\widehat V_{\mathrm{eff}}=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
(\widehat\phi_i-\overline{\widehat\phi})^2,
\qquad
\overline{\widehat\phi}=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat\phi_i,
\]
and report \(\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha}\).

definitions.name: Finite-support published-bound gap plug-in
definitions.construction:
For a declared comparator rule \(z\in\{\mathrm{OVS},\mathrm{const}\}\), let \(b_z(P)\) denote the law-dependent loading obtained from \(\Omega(P)\) by the corresponding Moore--Penrose KKT rule; it is not held fixed as the law varies.  Its loss relative to the published OVS bound is
\[
\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},z}(P)
=\operatorname{Var}_P\{b_z(P)'\Psi_P(O)\}-V_{\mathrm{OVS}}(P).
\tag{G1}
\]
For pointwise inference, suppose \(X\) has fixed support \(\{x_1,\ldots,x_D\}\).  Define the observable finite vector \(U(O)\) by stacking, separately, all coordinates
\[
U_d^X=\mathbf 1\{X=x_d\},
\qquad
U^{(0)}_{d,a,s}=\mathbf 1\{X=x_d,G=a,S=s\},
\tag{G2}
\]
\[
U^{(1,u)}_{d,a,s}=U^{(0)}_{d,a,s}\Delta Y_u,
\qquad
U^{(2,u,v)}_{d,a,s}=U^{(0)}_{d,a,s}\Delta Y_u\Delta Y_v,
\tag{G3}
\]
for every support point, every retained cohort--eligibility cell \((a,s)\in\mathcal G\times\{0,1\}\), and \(u,v\in\{2,\ldots,T\}\).  Let \(d_\mu\) be the number of stacked coordinates and \(\mu(P)=E_P[U(O)]\).  The separate coordinates \(U_d^X\) reconstruct every support mass exactly.  The remaining coordinates reconstruct all conditional cell probabilities, first moments, and second cross-moments, hence reconstruct \(p,m,\pi,\theta,\Psi,\Omega,Z^{\mathrm{OVS}},K_{\mathrm{OVS}},r_{\mathrm{OVS}}\).

Let \(b^{\mathrm{ref}}\) put weight \(\omega_k\) on \((k,c_0(k))\) and zero on the other score coordinates.  For every moment vector in the overlap domain define
\[
F_z(\mu)=b_z(\mu)'\Omega(\mu)b_z(\mu)
-\left\{b^{\mathrm{ref}\prime}\Omega(\mu)b^{\mathrm{ref}}
-\sum_{d=1}^D P_\mu(X=x_d)
r_{\mathrm{OVS},\mu}(x_d)'K_{\mathrm{OVS},\mu}(x_d)^\dagger
r_{\mathrm{OVS},\mu}(x_d)\right\}.
\tag{G4}
\]
Let \(F_z^\sharp\) denote the locally selected-rank branch of \(F_z\).  At the true moment define
\[
\xi_z(O)=DF_z^\sharp\{\mu(P)\}'[U(O)-\mu(P)].
\tag{G5}
\]
Every inverse in (G4), including an indefinite comparator KKT inverse, is operationally replaced by the spectral inverse that retains exactly eigenvalues satisfying \(|\lambda|>\tau_n\).  Denote the resulting map by \(F_{z,\tau_n}\).  With \(\widehat\mu=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nU(O_i)\), define
\[
\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}=F_{z,\tau_n}(\widehat\mu).
\tag{G6}
\]
Let \(\widehat d_z\) be the analytic derivative of the selected-rank branch of \(F_z\) at \(\widehat\mu\), put
\[
\widehat\xi_{z,i}=\widehat d_z'\{U(O_i)-\widehat\mu\},
\qquad
\widehat V_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat\xi_{z,i}^2,
\tag{G7}
\]
and set
\[
T_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}
=\frac{\sqrt n\{\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}-\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},z}(P)\}}
{\sqrt{\widehat V_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}}}.
\tag{G8}
\]

definitions.name: Bounded binary-covariate strict-gain family
definitions.construction: Set \(T=3\), \(\mathcal K=\{(2,2),(2,3)\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,2)}=\{3,\infty\}\), and \(\mathcal J_{(2,3)}=\{\infty\}\). Draw \(X\) uniformly on \(\{-1,1\}\), and draw \((G,S)\) uniformly on \(\{2,3,\infty\}\times\{0,1\}\) conditional on \(X\). Conditional on \(X=x\) and \(G=a\), draw \((U^{\mathrm w},V^{\mathrm w})\in\{-1,1\}^2\) with probability \(\{1+\rho_a(x)U^{\mathrm w}V^{\mathrm w}\}/4\), where \(\rho_2(x)=\rho_3(x)=0\) and \(\rho_{\infty}(x)=xr\). Put \(Z^{\mathrm w}=(0,U^{\mathrm w}/8,(U^{\mathrm w}+V^{\mathrm w})/8)^{\prime}\), define \(Y_t(a,s)=Z_t^{\mathrm w}+\delta s\mathbf 1\{a<\infty\}\mathbf 1\{t\ge a\}\), and set \(Y_t=Y_t(G,S)\). The resulting full-data law is \(Q^{\mathrm{bin}}_{r,\delta}\).

definitions.name: Published-normal rank-adaptive spectral handle
definitions.construction:
For the published normal system, form cross-fitted spectral projectors of \(\widehat K_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}(x)\) and regularized candidate coefficients from \(\widehat r_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}(x)\) over a threshold grid whose deterministic scale is \(\lambda_n\).  Compare the candidate projections across adjacent retained eigenspaces by a Lepski-type stability rule and calibrate critical values jointly over the retained-rank candidates.  This handle acts on the published canonical-projection coefficient
\[
\alpha_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x)=K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x)^\dagger r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x),
\]
not on the aggregate loading \(b^\star\) or the aggregate contrast operator \(H\).  A uniform theorem based on the handle must specify a class of local law sequences \((P_n)\), quantitative envelopes for the positive eigenvalues of \(K_{\mathrm{OVS},P_n}(X)\) and for all nuisance and conditional-moment errors relative to \(\lambda_n\), and a nonvacuity criterion stated through interval length or local power.  At every fixed finite-support law with separated positive rank, the selected center and interval are required to be asymptotically equivalent to the existing \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}\) and its Wald interval.  Rank changes of the comparator Moore--Penrose KKT systems are outside this handle and belong to a separate efficiency-gap inference extension.

definitions.name: Localized period-specific normal projection
definitions.construction:
Let \(\mathscr E_{\mathrm{loc}}\) contain every nonzero triple \(e=(u,c,c')\) for which there exist \(k=(g,t)\), \(k'=(g,t')\in\mathcal K\) with the same \(g\), \(u\in\{g,\ldots,\min(t,t')\}\), \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), and \(c'\in\mathcal J_{k'}\).  Associate the formal cell-incidence row
\[
\rho_e=e_{(c,1,u)}-e_{(c,0,u)}-e_{(c',1,u)}+e_{(c',0,u)}.
\]
The deterministic set \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{per}}\) is the lexicographically first maximal linearly independent subcollection of these rows.  Define \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\) from these coordinates by the residual formula already displayed in this definition, and set
\[
\psi_P^0=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\omega_k\Psi_{k,c_0(k),P},\quad
K_P(X)=E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}Z_P^{\mathrm{per}\prime}\mid X],\quad
r_P(X)=E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\psi_P^0\mid X],
\]
\[
p_{\mathrm{per},P}=r_P(X)'K_P(X)^\dagger Z_P^{\mathrm{per}},\quad
\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}=\psi_P^0-p_{\mathrm{per},P},\quad
V_{\mathrm{can}}=E_P[\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}^2].
\]
At a fixed finite-support conditional-mean interior law satisfying overlap and the fourth-moment condition, Theorem \(\ref{thm:observable-equivalence}\) identifies these as the localized tangent-normal projection, canonical gradient, and efficiency bound.  Outside that proved regime the same formulas denote the localized normal-span projection objects, without a tangent-exhaustion or canonicality assertion.  The definitions of \(\phi_{\mathrm{agg},P}\), \(V_{\mathrm{agg}}\), and \(\Delta_{\mathrm{normal}}=V_{\mathrm{agg}}-V_{\mathrm{can}}\) are unchanged.

definitions.name: Orthogonal complete-normal restriction signal
definitions.construction:
For a retained cohort \(a\) and period \(u\), set
\[
d_{a,u}(x)=m_{a,1,u}(x)-m_{a,0,u}(x).
\]
For \(e=(u,c,c')\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{per}}\), define the conditional restriction level
\[
g_e(x)=d_{c,u}(x)-d_{c',u}(x).
\]
For a candidate nuisance \(\widetilde\eta=(\widetilde p,\widetilde m)\) whose retained propensity coordinates are positive, let
\[
Z_e(O;\widetilde\eta)=
\frac{\mathbf 1_{c,1}}{\widetilde p_{c,1}(X)}\{\Delta Y_u-\widetilde m_{c,1,u}(X)\}
-\frac{\mathbf 1_{c,0}}{\widetilde p_{c,0}(X)}\{\Delta Y_u-\widetilde m_{c,0,u}(X)\}
-\frac{\mathbf 1_{c',1}}{\widetilde p_{c',1}(X)}\{\Delta Y_u-\widetilde m_{c',1,u}(X)\}
+\frac{\mathbf 1_{c',0}}{\widetilde p_{c',0}(X)}\{\Delta Y_u-\widetilde m_{c',0,u}(X)\},
\]
and
\[
S_e(O;\widetilde\eta)=
\widetilde d_{c,u}(X)-\widetilde d_{c',u}(X)+Z_e(O;\widetilde\eta),
\qquad
\widetilde d_{a,u}=\widetilde m_{a,1,u}-\widetilde m_{a,0,u}.
\]
Stack these coordinates in \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{per}}\)-order as \(S^{\mathrm{per}}(O;\widetilde\eta)\), using the zero-dimensional convention when \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{per}}\) is empty.

definitions.name: Clean-through-terminal localized observed model
definitions.construction:
Let \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{loc}}\) be the class of observed laws \(P\) satisfying, for every \(k=(g,t)\), \(k'=(g,t')\in\mathcal K\) with the same target cohort, every \(u\in\{g,\ldots,\min(t,t')\}\), every \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), and every \(c'\in\mathcal J_{k'}\),
\[
d_{c,u}(X)=d_{c',u}(X)\quad P_X\text{-almost surely}.
\]
This is the larger clean-through-terminal localized equality model.  It omits OVS rows involving a cohort that is clean at \(u\) but not through a selected terminal period.

definitions.name: Conditional-mean interior law
definitions.construction: An observed law is a conditional-mean interior point if, for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\) and every retained cohort--eligibility cell \((a,s)\), the conditional mean of the finite vector \((\Delta Y_2,\ldots,\Delta Y_T)\) lies in the relative interior of the closed convex hull of its conditional essential support given \((G,S,X)=(a,s,x)\).  Relative interior is taken in the affine hull of that support, so degenerate conditional coordinates create no unattainable tangent direction.

definitions.name: Published OVS complete normal projection
definitions.construction:
For every \(u\in\{2,\ldots,T\}\) for which some finite \(g\in\mathcal G\) satisfies \(g\le u\), let \(\mathscr E_{\mathrm{OVS}}\) contain all nonzero rows indexed by \(e=(u,c,c')\) with distinct \(c,c'\in\mathcal C_u^{\mathrm{OVS}}\):
\[
\rho_e=e_{(c,1,u)}-e_{(c,0,u)}-e_{(c',1,u)}+e_{(c',0,u)}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{OVS}}\) be the lexicographically first maximal linearly independent subcollection of these formal rows.  For \(e=(u,c,c')\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{OVS}}\), set
\[
Z^{\mathrm{OVS}}_{e,P}(O)=
\frac{\mathbf 1_{c,1}}{p_{c,1}(X)}\{\Delta Y_u-m_{c,1,u}(X)\}
-\frac{\mathbf 1_{c,0}}{p_{c,0}(X)}\{\Delta Y_u-m_{c,0,u}(X)\}
-\frac{\mathbf 1_{c',1}}{p_{c',1}(X)}\{\Delta Y_u-m_{c',1,u}(X)\}
+\frac{\mathbf 1_{c',0}}{p_{c',0}(X)}\{\Delta Y_u-m_{c',0,u}(X)\},
\]
and stack these coordinates as \(Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\).  With \(\psi_P^0\) from Definition \(\ref{def:complete-normal-projection}\), define
\[
K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)=E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}\prime}\mid X],\qquad
r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)=E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\psi_P^0\mid X],
\]
\[
p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}=r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)'K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)^\dagger Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}},\qquad
\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}=\psi_P^0-p_{\mathrm{OVS},P},\qquad
V_{\mathrm{OVS}}=E_P[\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}^2].
\]
Use zero-dimensional conventions when there is no nonzero OVS row, and set \(\Delta_{\mathrm{model}}=V_{\mathrm{can}}-V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\).

definitions.name: Orthogonal published OVS normal signal
definitions.construction:
For \(e=(u,c,c')\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{OVS}}\), set
\[
g_e^{\mathrm{OVS}}(x)=d_{c,u}(x)-d_{c',u}(x).
\]
For a candidate nuisance \(\widetilde\eta=(\widetilde p,\widetilde m)\) with positive retained propensity coordinates, define \(Z_e^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O;\widetilde\eta)\) by replacing \((p,m)\) with \((\widetilde p,\widetilde m)\) in Definition \(\ref{def:ovs-normal-projection}\), and put
\[
S_e^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O;\widetilde\eta)
=\widetilde d_{c,u}(X)-\widetilde d_{c',u}(X)
+Z_e^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O;\widetilde\eta),
\qquad
\widetilde d_{a,u}=\widetilde m_{a,1,u}-\widetilde m_{a,0,u}.
\]
Stack the coordinates in \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{OVS}}\)-order as \(S^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O;\widetilde\eta)\), with the zero-dimensional convention.

statements.statement:
Let \(\mathcal C_u^{\mathrm{OVS}}=\{c\in\mathcal G:c>u\}\), where \(\infty>u\), and let \(d_{a,u}(x)=m_{a,1,u}(x)-m_{a,0,u}(x)\).  Under retained-cell overlap, an observed law \(P\), with otherwise arbitrary covariate support, admits a full-data extension \(Q\in\mathcal M\) if and only if
\[
d_{c,u}(X)=d_{c',u}(X)
\quad P_X\text{-almost surely}
\tag{1}
\]
for every \(u\in\{2,\ldots,T\}\) for which some finite \(g\in\mathcal G\) satisfies \(g\le u\), and every \(c,c'\in\mathcal C_u^{\mathrm{OVS}}\).  Thus the published class uses every cohort clean at period \(u\), including a cohort with \(u<c\le t\) that is unavailable as a single clean-through-\(t\) comparison for a terminal target \((g,t)\).

Suppose in addition that the fourth-moment condition holds, that \(X\) has fixed finite support \(\{x_1,\ldots,x_D\}\) with \(P(X=x_d)>0\) for every \(d\), and that \(P\) is a conditional-mean interior law.  Then the published observed tangent orthocomplement is
\[
\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp
=\overline{\{a(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O):a\text{ measurable and }
E_P[(a(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O))^2]<\infty\}}^{L_2(P)}.
\tag{2}
\]
At the same law, the larger localized observed model \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{loc}}\) of Definition \(\ref{def:local-observed-model}\), which retains only cohorts clean through a target's terminal period, has
\[
\mathcal T_P^\perp
=\overline{\{a(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}(O):a\text{ measurable and }
E_P[(a(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}(O))^2]<\infty\}}^{L_2(P)}.
\tag{3}
\]
Every local formal row is an OVS row.  Consequently
\[
\mathcal C_P\subseteq\mathcal T_P^\perp
\subseteq\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp,
\qquad
\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}\subseteq\mathcal T_P.
\tag{4}
\]
The cumulative equalities \(q_{k,c}=q_{k,c_0(k)}\) are necessary in both models but, whenever a target spans more than one period, do not in general imply even the localized period-specific equalities.  No tangent-exhaustion assertion is made here for continuously distributed \(X\).
statements.justification: The theorem proves the full-data image for arbitrary covariate support and, separately, proves literal OVS and localized tangent exhaustion at fixed finite-support conditional-mean interior laws by an explicit affine-support right inverse and exact bounded likelihood tilts.
statements.gap: Continuous-covariate tangent exhaustion would require a measurable, sufficiently bounded conditional right inverse; it is not claimed.
statements.consumer: The fixed-support canonical-gradient and inference results use the exhaustive period-admissible cohort--period normal system.
statements.proof_tex:
Write
\[
D^0_{a,u}(x)=E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,1)\mid G=a,S=1,X=x]
-E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,0)\mid G=a,S=0,X=x].
\]
We first prove necessity of (1).  Fix \(u\), a finite \(g\le u\), and \(c\in\mathcal C_u^{\mathrm{OVS}}\).  Because \(c>u\), Assumption \(\ref{ass:no-anticipation}\), applied at \(u-1\) and \(u\), and Assumption \(\ref{ass:consistency}\) give
\[
E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,1)\mid G=c,S=1,X]=m_{c,1,u}(X).
\tag{5}
\]
Assumptions \(\ref{ass:no-ineligible-effect}\) and \(\ref{ass:consistency}\) similarly give
\[
E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,0)\mid G=c,S=0,X]=m_{c,0,u}(X).
\tag{6}
\]
Thus \(D^0_{c,u}(X)=d_{c,u}(X)\).  Assumption \(\ref{ass:conditional-parallel-gap}\), applied with comparison \(c\) and then with comparison \(c'\), yields
\[
d_{c,u}(X)=D^0_{g,u}(X)=d_{c',u}(X),
\]
which is (1).  This step uses the published condition \(c>u\), not the stronger condition \(c>t\).

Conversely, suppose (1) holds.  Since \(\infty\in\mathcal C_u^{\mathrm{OVS}}\), define the common observable gap
\[
\delta_u(x)=d_{\infty,u}(x).
\tag{7}
\]
Equation (1) gives \(d_{c,u}(x)=\delta_u(x)\) for every \(c>u\) at every period indexed by a published restriction.  We construct a full-data extension on the observed probability space, enlarged only by independent auxiliary variables if desired.  For every unit, set \(Y_v(a,0)=Y_v\) for all \(a\in\mathcal G\) and \(v\in\mathcal T\).  On units with \(S=0\), also set every eligible potential path equal to the observed path.  On a unit with \(S=1\) and finite factual cohort \(a\), set \(Y_v(a,1)=Y_v\), set \(Y_v(\infty,1)=Y_v\) for \(v<a\), and recursively set, for \(v\ge a\),
\[
\Delta Y_v(\infty,1)=m_{a,0,v}(X)+\delta_v(X)+\xi_{a,v},
\qquad
E_Q[\xi_{a,v}\mid G=a,S=1,X]=0.
\tag{8}
\]
The choice \(\xi_{a,v}=0\) is admissible.  On units with \((G,S)=(\infty,1)\), take the observed path as the never-enabled eligible path.  On eligible units, define every remaining nonfactual finite-cohort eligible path to equal the specified never-enabled eligible path.  The array is finite because \(T\) and \(\mathcal G\) are finite, so this prescription defines every potential-outcome coordinate, gives \(Y_v(G,S)=Y_v\), and preserves the observed marginal.

The construction on \(S=0\) proves no effect on ineligible units and consistency there.  The factual-path assignment proves consistency on \(S=1\).  For a finite factual cohort \(a\), the equality of its factual and never-enabled paths before \(a\) proves Assumption \(\ref{ass:no-anticipation}\).  For every finite \(g\le u\), (8) and the ineligible construction imply
\[
D^0_{g,u}(X)=m_{g,0,u}(X)+\delta_u(X)-m_{g,0,u}(X)=\delta_u(X).
\tag{9}
\]
For every \(c>u\), the constructed never-enabled path equals the observed path at \(u-1\) and \(u\); hence (5)--(7) give \(D^0_{c,u}(X)=\delta_u(X)\).  Equation (9) is therefore every restriction in Assumption \(\ref{ass:conditional-parallel-gap}\).  The constructed law belongs to \(\mathcal M\), proving sufficiency.  This construction did not restrict the support of \(X\), so the equivalence part of the theorem is general in the covariate law.

We now prove tangent exhaustion under the stated finite-support condition.  Put \(V=(\Delta Y_2,\ldots,\Delta Y_T)'\) and \(C=(G,S)\).  For every retained cell and period define
\[
U_{a,s,u}(O)=\frac{\mathbf 1_{a,s}}{p_{a,s}(X)}
\{\Delta Y_u-m_{a,s,u}(X)\}.
\tag{10}
\]
Assumption \(\ref{ass:cell-overlap}\) and Assumption \(\ref{ass:fourth-moment}\) imply \(U_{a,s,u}\in L_2(P)\); Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) gives \(E_P[U_{a,s,u}\mid X]=0\).  If \(P_\epsilon\) is a regular dominated observed submodel with score \(s\in L_2^0(P)\), differentiating the conditional numerator and denominator gives
\[
\dot m_{a,s_0,u}(x)
=E_P[U_{a,s_0,u}(O)s(O)\mid X=x].
\tag{11}
\]
Indeed, the denominator derivative subtracts \(m_{a,s_0,u}(x)E_P[s\mid G=a,S=s_0,X=x]\) from the numerator derivative, which is exactly the centered residual on the right.  Therefore, for an indexed row \(e=(u,c,c')\),
\[
\dot d_{c,u}(x)-\dot d_{c',u}(x)
=E_P[Z^{\mathrm{OVS}}_{e,P}(O)s(O)\mid X=x].
\tag{12}
\]

Because \(X\) has support \(\{x_1,\ldots,x_D\}\), define the finite-dimensional continuous operator
\[
\mathscr D_{\mathrm{OVS}}s
=\bigl(E_P[Z^{\mathrm{OVS}}_{e,P}s\mid X=x_d]
 :e\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{OVS}},\ 1\le d\le D\bigr).
\tag{13}
\]
Differentiating (1) along any in-model regular submodel and using (12) proves
\(\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}\subseteq\ker\mathscr D_{\mathrm{OVS}}\).

We prove the reverse inclusion by an explicit finite-cell construction.  Fix a cell \(j=(a,s,x_d)\), write \(\mu_j=E_P[V\mid C=(a,s),X=x_d]\), and let
\[
\mathcal A_j=\operatorname{span}\{v-\mu_j:v\in
\operatorname{ess\,supp}(V\mid C=(a,s),X=x_d)\}.
\tag{14}
\]
This is the linear part of the affine support appearing in Definition \(\ref{def:conditional-mean-interior}\).  If its dimension is \(q_j>0\), choose essential-support points \(v_{j,0},\ldots,v_{j,q_j}\) whose differences span \(\mathcal A_j\).  Choose sufficiently small bounded neighborhoods \(B_{j,\ell}\) of these points.  Each has positive conditional probability by the definition of essential support, and the neighborhoods may be chosen so that their conditional means \(\bar v_{j,\ell}=E_P[V\mid V\in B_{j,\ell},C=(a,s),X=x_d]\) retain affine independence.  The bounded, cell-centered functions
\[
w_{j,\ell}(V)=
\frac{\mathbf 1\{V\in B_{j,\ell}\}}
{P(V\in B_{j,\ell}\mid C=(a,s),X=x_d)}
-
\frac{\mathbf 1\{V\in B_{j,0}\}}
{P(V\in B_{j,0}\mid C=(a,s),X=x_d)},
\quad 1\le\ell\le q_j,
\tag{15}
\]
satisfy
\[
E_P[w_{j,\ell}\mid C=(a,s),X=x_d]=0,
\qquad
E_P[(V-\mu_j)w_{j,\ell}mid C=(a,s),X=x_d]
=\bar v_{j,\ell}-\bar v_{j,0}.
\tag{16}
\]
Thus (15)--(16) give an explicit linear right inverse \(J_j\) from \(\mathcal A_j\) into bounded cell-centered likelihood scores.  If \(q_j=0\), take the unique zero map.  The relative-interior clause ensures that all admissible mean directions are interpreted in \(\mathcal A_j\); no direction orthogonal to the affine support is introduced.

Let \(\mathcal A_d\) be the direct sum of the finitely many \(\mathcal A_j\)'s at \(x_d\), let \(J_d\) be the direct sum of the maps \(J_j\), and let \(R_d:\mathcal A_d\to\mathbb R^{|\mathcal E_{\mathrm{OVS}}|}\) take a collection of cell-mean shifts to the signed eligibility-gap row shifts in (12).  In fixed bases, \(R_d\) is an ordinary finite matrix.  Hence its Moore--Penrose inverse is a right inverse on its range:
\[
R_dR_d^\dagger y=y,
\qquad y\in\operatorname{range}R_d.
\tag{17}
\]
Define \(B_d=J_dR_d^\dagger\).  Equations (16)--(17) show that \(B_dy\) is bounded and cell-centered and that its induced restriction derivative is exactly \(y\).  Since there are finitely many support points and cells, the operator norms of all \(B_d\)'s are bounded by one finite, law-dependent constant.

Take any \(s\in\ker\mathscr D_{\mathrm{OVS}}\), and decompose it orthogonally as
\[
s=s_X+s_C+s_Y,
\qquad
s_X=E_P[s\mid X],
\quad s_C=E_P[s\mid C,X]-E_P[s\mid X],
\quad s_Y=s-E_P[s\mid C,X].
\tag{18}
\]
Because both \(X\) and \(C\) have finite support and every retained cell has positive probability by overlap, \(s_X\) and \(s_C\) are bounded.  Only \(s_Y\) changes conditional outcome means, because residuals in (10) have conditional mean zero given \((C,X)\).  Let
\[
v_j=\max(-j,\min(s_Y,j))
-E_P[\max(-j,\min(s_Y,j))\mid C,X].
\tag{19}
\]
Then \(v_j\) is bounded and cell-centered and \(v_j\to s_Y\) in \(L_2(P)\).  At \(X=x_d\), let \(L_dv_j\) be the restriction derivative induced by the cell-mean shifts of \(v_j\), and define
\[
u_j=v_j-B_XL_Xv_j.
\tag{20}
\]
The vector \(L_dv_j\) belongs to \(\operatorname{range}R_d\), so (17) gives \(L_du_j=0\) exactly.  Continuity of (13), \(L_ds_Y=0\), and the finite bound on \(B_d\) imply
\[
\|u_j-s_Y\|_{P,2}
\le \|v_j-s_Y\|_{P,2}
+C\|\mathscr D_{\mathrm{OVS}}v_j\|
\longrightarrow0.
\tag{21}
\]
Consequently \(s^{(j)}=s_X+s_C+u_j\) is bounded, belongs to \(\ker\mathscr D_{\mathrm{OVS}}\), and converges to \(s\) in \(L_2(P)\).

For fixed \(j\) and sufficiently small \(|\epsilon|\), define the likelihood ratio
\[
\frac{dP_{\epsilon,j}}{dP}
=\{1+\epsilon s_X(X)\}
 \{1+\epsilon s_C(C,X)\}
 \{1+\epsilon u_j(O)\}.
\tag{22}
\]
Every factor is strictly positive for small enough \(|\epsilon|\).  The three centering identities in (18)--(20) show successively that the factors integrate to one for the marginal law of \(X\), the conditional law of \(C\) given \(X\), and the conditional law of \(Y\) given \((C,X)\).  Thus (22) is a dominated probability submodel.  Its score at zero is \(s_X+s_C+u_j=s^{(j)}\), and its square-root likelihood ratio has the uniform expansion
\[
\sqrt{dP_{\epsilon,j}/dP}
=1+\frac{\epsilon}{2}s^{(j)}+O(\epsilon^2),
\tag{23}
\]
so the submodel is differentiable in quadratic mean.

Under (22), a conditional outcome mean changes exactly, not merely to first order:
\[
E_{P_{\epsilon,j}}[V\mid C,X]
=E_P[V\mid C,X]
+\epsilon E_P[(V-E_P[V\mid C,X])u_j\mid C,X].
\tag{24}
\]
The other two factors change only the marginal law of \(X\) and the cell probabilities.  Since \(L_du_j=0\), substituting (24) leaves every basis-row equality exact for all sufficiently small \(\epsilon\).  Definition \(\ref{def:ovs-normal-projection}\) selects a maximal linearly independent collection of the formal OVS rows, so every omitted row is a fixed linear combination of those basis rows and is also exactly zero.  The already proved sufficiency construction lifts every \(P_{\epsilon,j}\) to a full-data law in \(\mathcal M\).  Boundedness of (22) preserves the fourth moment, and overlap persists locally because all cell probabilities are multiplied by positive factors uniformly close to one.  Hence every \(s^{(j)}\) is the score of a regular in-model submodel.  Taking the \(L_2(P)\) limit in (21) proves
\[
\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}=ker\mathscr D_{\mathrm{OVS}}.
\tag{25}
\]

Let \(\mathcal N_{\mathrm{OVS}}\) denote the closed space on the right of (2).  If \(s\perp\mathcal N_{\mathrm{OVS}}\), then for every coordinate \(e\) and every support indicator \(\mathbf 1\{X=x_d\}\),
\[
E_P[\mathbf 1\{X=x_d\}Z^{\mathrm{OVS}}_{e,P}s]=0.
\]
Since \(P(X=x_d)>0\), this is equivalent to every coordinate of \(\mathscr D_{\mathrm{OVS}}s\) being zero.  Conversely, \(\mathscr D_{\mathrm{OVS}}s=0\) makes \(s\) orthogonal to every measurable multiple of \(Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\) and hence to its closure.  Therefore
\[
\mathcal N_{\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp
=\ker\mathscr D_{\mathrm{OVS}}
=\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}.
\]
Taking orthogonal complements of closed subspaces proves (2).  Repeating (10)--(25) with the finite local row matrix in Definition \(\ref{def:complete-normal-projection}\) proves (3).

If a local row is indexed through targets \(k=(g,t)\), \(k'=(g,t')\), period \(u\le\min(t,t')\), and comparisons \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), \(c'\in\mathcal J_{k'}\), then \(c>t\ge u\) and \(c'>t'\ge u\).  Hence every local row is a published OVS row.  This proves \(\mathcal T_P^\perp\subseteq\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp\), and orthogonal complementation gives the tangent inclusion in (4).

For two comparisons in one target block, direct subtraction of Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) gives
\[
R_{k,c,P}-R_{k,c',P}
=-\frac{p_{g,1}(X)}{\pi_{g,1}}
\sum_{u=g}^t Z_{u;c,c',P}.
\tag{26}
\]
Every summand is a local formal row, so its residual contrast is a fixed linear combination of the independent coordinates stacked in \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\).  Since each column of \(N\) has coefficients summing to zero within every target block, \(N'R_P\) is a finite linear combination of differences of the form (26).  Thus every square-integrable measurable aggregate contrast is in \(\mathcal T_P^\perp\); taking closure proves \(\mathcal C_P\subseteq\mathcal T_P^\perp\) and completes (4).

Finally, let \(T=4\), \(\mathcal K=\{(2,3)\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,3)}=\{4,\infty\}\), and let \(X\) be degenerate.  Give every cohort--eligibility cell positive probability and choose bounded conditional outcome distributions with
\[
d_{4,2}=1,\qquad d_{4,3}=-1,
\qquad d_{\infty,2}=d_{\infty,3}=0.
\]
Then \(\sum_{u=2}^3d_{4,u}=\sum_{u=2}^3d_{\infty,u}=0\), so the cumulative comparison equality holds, while both period-specific equalities fail.  Equation (1) and the definition of the localized model therefore exclude this observed law from both models.  This supplies the asserted witness.

statements.statement:
Let \(P\) satisfy the observable clean-comparison equalities and admit \(Q\in\mathcal M\) that induces \(P\), with mean no anticipation imposed on every retained finite target or comparison cohort.  For every \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\) and every \(c\in\mathcal J_k\),
\[
q_{k,c}(X)=E_Q[Y_t(g,1)-Y_t(\infty,1)\mid G=g,S=1,X]\qquad P_X\text{-almost surely}.
\]
Consequently
\[
\theta_k(P)=E_Q[Y_t(g,1)-Y_t(\infty,1)\mid G=g,S=1],\qquad
\tau_\omega(P)=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\omega_k\theta_k(P),
\]
and the centered ratio-functional OVS score is
\[
\Psi_{k,c,P}(O)=R_{k,c,P}(O)-\frac{\theta_k(P)}{\pi_{g,1}}\mathbf 1\{G=g,S=1\}.
\]
statements.justification: This fixes the causal target before any efficiency calculation and retains the denominator derivative through \(\pi_{g,1}\).
statements.gap: Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna (2025, Theorem 4.1) establish identification under their conditional-mean no-anticipation and period-by-period DDD parallel-trends conditions; this lemma records the exact reduction used here rather than claiming novelty.
statements.consumer: Every later tangent, score, and package result targets the same prespecified aggregate rather than a data-adaptive estimand.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), and \(u\in\{g,\ldots,t\}\).  Because \(P\) is induced by \(Q\), consistency implies
\[
m_{g,1,u}(X)
=E_Q[\Delta Y_u(g,1)\mid G=g,S=1,X].
\tag{C1}
\]
No effect on ineligible units, followed by consistency, implies
\[
\begin{aligned}
m_{g,0,u}(X)
&=E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,0)\mid G=g,S=0,X],\\
m_{c,0,u}(X)
&=E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,0)\mid G=c,S=0,X].
\end{aligned}
\tag{C2}
\]
Since \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), one has \(c>t\ge u\).  If \(c\) is finite, mean no anticipation for cohort \(c\), applied at both \(u<c\) and \(u-1<c\), and consistency give
\[
m_{c,1,u}(X)
=E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,1)\mid G=c,S=1,X].
\tag{C3}
\]
If \(c=\infty\), (C3) follows directly from consistency.  Define the untreated eligibility gap
\[
B_{a,u}(X)
=E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,1)\mid G=a,S=1,X]
-E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,0)\mid G=a,S=0,X].
\]
The conditional parallel-gap assumption applies because \(u\ge g\) and \(c>u\), and hence gives \(B_{g,u}(X)=B_{c,u}(X)\) almost surely.  Using (C1)--(C3) and this equality,
\[
\begin{aligned}
&m_{g,1,u}(X)-m_{g,0,u}(X)-m_{c,1,u}(X)+m_{c,0,u}(X)\\
&\quad=E_Q[\Delta Y_u(g,1)\mid G=g,S=1,X]
-E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,1)\mid G=g,S=1,X]\\
&\quad=E_Q[\Delta Y_u(g,1)-\Delta Y_u(\infty,1)\mid G=g,S=1,X].
\end{aligned}
\tag{C4}
\]
Summing (C4) over \(u=g,\ldots,t\), using the definition of \(q_{k,c}\), linearity of conditional expectation, and telescoping of the potential-outcome increments yields
\[
q_{k,c}(X)
=E_Q\!\left[
Y_t(g,1)-Y_t(\infty,1)
-\{Y_{g-1}(g,1)-Y_{g-1}(\infty,1)\}
\mathrel{\middle|}G=g,S=1,X\right].
\tag{C5}
\]
Mean no anticipation for the finite target cohort \(g\) at the pretreatment date \(g-1<g\) makes the conditional expectation of the braced term zero.  Therefore
\[
q_{k,c}(X)
=E_Q[Y_t(g,1)-Y_t(\infty,1)\mid G=g,S=1,X]
\quad P_X\text{-almost surely}.
\tag{C6}
\]
This argument also shows that the right-hand side is independent of the chosen clean comparison \(c\).

Cell overlap and the definition of \(\pi_{g,1}\) give
\[
\pi_{g,1}=E_P[p_{g,1}(X)]\ge\varepsilon>0,
\tag{C7}
\]
so the ratio defining \(\theta_k(P)\) is well defined.  The conditional law of \(X\) given \(G=g,S=1\) has Radon--Nikodym derivative \(p_{g,1}(X)/\pi_{g,1}\) with respect to \(P_X\).  Multiplying (C6) by that derivative and integrating therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\theta_k(P)
&=\frac{E_P[p_{g,1}(X)q_{k,c}(X)]}{\pi_{g,1}}\\
&=E_Q[Y_t(g,1)-Y_t(\infty,1)\mid G=g,S=1].
\end{aligned}
\tag{C8}
\]
The asserted formula for \(\tau_\omega(P)\) follows by multiplying (C8) by the prespecified \(\omega_k\), summing over the finite set \(\mathcal K\), and using the definition of \(\tau_\omega\).

Finally, for every cell \((a,s)\), the definition of \(m_{a,s,u}\) gives
\[
E_P[\mathbf 1_{a,s}e_{a,s,k}(O)\mid X]=0.
\tag{C9}
\]
All inverse cell probabilities in Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) are finite by overlap.  Hence (C9), the displayed formula for \(R_{k,c,P}\), and (C6) imply
\[
E_P[\Psi_{k,c,P}(O)\mid X]
=\frac{p_{g,1}(X)}{\pi_{g,1}}
\{q_{k,c}(X)-\theta_k(P)\}.
\tag{C10}
\]
More directly, subtracting the ratio-denominator derivative in that definition gives the pointwise identity
\[
\Psi_{k,c,P}(O)
=R_{k,c,P}(O)
-\frac{\theta_k(P)}{\pi_{g,1}}\mathbf 1\{G=g,S=1\},
\]
which is the claimed centered ratio-functional score.

statements.statement: Under fixed contrast rank, the conditional minimizer has the measurable quotient-space representation \[b^{\star}(x)=b^0-NH(x)^{\dagger}N^{\prime}\Gamma(x)b^0,\] satisfies \(A^{\prime}b^{\star}(x)=\omega\) and \(N^{\prime}\Gamma(x)b^{\star}(x)=0\), and is unique modulo \(\ker\Gamma(x)\cap\ker A^{\prime}\). The range relation \(N^{\prime}\Gamma(x)b^0\in\operatorname{range}H(x)\) follows from positive semidefiniteness and is not assumed. If \(\Gamma(x)\) is positive definite, then \[b^{\star}(x)=\Gamma(x)^{-1}A\{A^{\prime}\Gamma(x)^{-1}A\}^{-1}\omega.\]
statements.justification: Redundant clean comparisons are economically natural, so the efficient loading must be invariant to null score coordinates.
statements.gap: Newey (2001, Theorem 5.2) handles singular conditional-moment covariance abstractly; the result here supplies the DDD affine-constraint quotient and its measurable fixed-rank form.
statements.consumer: The constrained solver used by the optional \(\texttt{triplediff}\) backend remains defined when retained score coordinates are redundant.
statements.proof_tex:
Because \(A\) has full column rank and the columns of \(N\) are an orthonormal basis of \(\ker(A')\), every feasible vector has a unique representation \(b=b^0+Nz\).  Suppress \(x\) and put \(g=N'\Gamma b^0\).  Then
\[
(b^0+Nz)'\Gamma(b^0+Nz)
=b^{0\prime}\Gamma b^0+2z'g+z'Hz.
\tag{O1}
\]
If \(v\in\ker H\), positive semidefiniteness gives
\[
0=v'Hv=(Nv)'\Gamma(Nv)=\|\Gamma^{1/2}Nv\|^2.
\]
Thus \(\Gamma Nv=0\) and \(v'g=(Nv)'\Gamma b^0=0\).  Since \(H\) is finite-dimensional and symmetric, \((\ker H)^\perp=\operatorname{range}H\), so \(g\in\operatorname{range}H\).  The normal equation \(Hz=-g\) is solvable, and its unique solution in \(\operatorname{range}H\) is \(z^\star=-H^\dagger g\).  Hence
\[
b^\star=b^0-NH^\dagger N'\Gamma b^0,
\quad A'b^\star=\omega,
\quad N'\Gamma b^\star=g-HH^\dagger g=0.
\tag{O2}
\]
Under fixed rank and the separated positive spectrum, \(H^\dagger\) is obtained by applying the Borel function \(z\mapsto z^{-1}\mathbf 1\{z\ge\kappa\}\) to the measurable symmetric matrix \(H\); therefore (O2) is measurable.  Two minimizers differ by \(Nv\) with \(v\in\ker H\), and the preceding calculation identifies this set with \(\ker\Gamma\cap\ker A'\).

If \(\Gamma\) is positive definite, the Lagrange equations are \(\Gamma b=A\lambda\) and \(A'b=\omega\).  Full column rank of \(A\) makes \(A'\Gamma^{-1}A\) positive definite.  Solving gives
\[
b=\Gamma^{-1}A(A'\Gamma^{-1}A)^{-1}\omega.
\]

statements.statement:
If \(X\) has fixed finite support with every support mass bounded below, and if the fixed-\(L\) folds satisfy \(\min_{1\le\ell\le L}|I_\ell^c|\ge c_Fn\) for some fixed \(c_F>0\), the foldwise cell-frequency estimator of the corrected shared-cell covariance \(\Gamma_P(X)=\operatorname{Cov}_P\{\Psi_P(O)\mid X\}\) satisfies
\[
\max_\ell\|\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}-\Gamma\|_{P_X,4,\mathrm{op}}
=O_P(n^{-1/2}+r_{p,n}+r_{m,n}).
\]
All conditional expectations used in a correctly specified one-step construction are estimated by the corresponding cell averages. If, in addition, contrast rank is fixed and its positive spectrum is separated, parametric first stages and \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\) with \(0<a<1/4\) give consistent rank recovery, \(r_{\Gamma,n}=O(n^{-1/2})\), and \(r_{b,n}=O(n^{-1/2+a})\), with \(r_{b,n}^2+r_{\Gamma,n}^2=o(n^{-1/2})\). The continuous-covariate \(L_4(P_X)\) rate in the original statement does not follow from only a conditional fourth moment for outcomes.
statements.justification: The proposition gives a checkable root-\(n\) shared-cell covariance rate for fixed finite covariate support.
statements.gap: No continuous-covariate \(L_4(P_X)\) covariance rate follows without additional smoothness and tail conditions.
statements.consumer: The finite-support implementation can learn \(\Gamma_P(X)\) for aggregate-loading and comparator diagnostics by cell frequencies.
statements.proof_tex:
Write the fixed support as \(\{x_1,\ldots,x_J\}\), where \(J<\infty\), and put \(\nu_j=P(X=x_j)\).  The proposed fold-balance condition and the support-mass hypothesis give constants \(c_F,\underline\nu>0\) such that
\[
 |I_\ell^c|\ge c_Fn,
 \qquad
 \min_{1\le j\le J}\nu_j\ge\underline\nu
 \tag{C1}
\]
for every fold and all \(n\).  Assumption \(\ref{ass:cell-overlap}\) then gives
\[
 P(X=x_j,G=a,S=s)=\nu_jp_{a,s}(x_j)
 \ge \underline\nu\varepsilon,
 \qquad
 \pi_{g,1}=E\{p_{g,1}(X)\}\ge\varepsilon.
 \tag{C2}
\]
Thus every denominator entering Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) is separated from zero.

We first give an explicit description of the cell-frequency implementation.  For each training complement \(I_\ell^c\), form the empirical averages of the finite collection
\[
 \mathbf 1\{X=x_j,G=a,S=s\},\quad
 \mathbf 1\{X=x_j,G=a,S=s\}\Delta Y_u,quad
 \mathbf 1\{X=x_j,G=a,S=s\}\Delta Y_u\Delta Y_v,
 \tag{C3}
\]
where \(j,a,s,u,v\) range over their fixed sets, together with the target-cell indicators \(\mathbf 1\{G=g,S=1\}\).  Divide the first-moment averages by the corresponding empirical cell frequencies to obtain \(\widehat m^{-\ell}\), use the empirical conditional cell shares for \(\widehat p^{-\ell}\), and use the empirical target shares for \(\widehat\pi^{-\ell}\).  Substitute these quantities in Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\), including its ratio correction, and take within-\(X\)-cell empirical first and second moments of that score.  Their difference is \(\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x_j)\).  On the event that an empirical denominator is smaller than half its population lower bound in (C2), define the corresponding ratio arbitrarily; the probability of this event tends to zero at the rate established below.  This makes the estimator a total measurable map of the training sample.

For every retained cell and period, Assumption \(\ref{ass:conditional-fourth-envelope}\) and the elementary conditional inequality
\[
 |E(\Delta Y_u\mid G=a,S=s,X)|^4
 \le E(|\Delta Y_u|^4\mid G=a,S=s,X)
 \tag{C4}
\]
bound \(m_{a,s,u}(X)\) uniformly.  Because \(T\), \(\mathcal G\), and \(\mathcal I\) are fixed and (C2) bounds every inverse propensity and target share, Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) and \(|z_1+\cdots+z_d|^4\le d^3\sum_h|z_h|^4\) imply
\[
 \sup_{1\le j\le J}E\{\|\Psi_P(O)\|^4\mid X=x_j\}<\infty.
 \tag{C5}
\]
Moreover, for any two periods,
\[
 E\{(\Delta Y_u\Delta Y_v)^2\mid G=a,S=s,X=x_j\}
 \le
 E(|\Delta Y_u|^4\mid G=a,S=s,X=x_j)^{1/2}
 E(|\Delta Y_v|^4\mid G=a,S=s,X=x_j)^{1/2},
 \tag{C6}
\]
so every variable in (C3) has finite variance, uniformly over the fixed index set.

Let \(\mu\) be the finite vector of population moments in (C3) and the target shares, and let \(\widehat\mu^{-\ell}\) be its training-sample version.  Independence in Assumption \(\ref{ass:crossfit-independence}\) is not needed for this within-training calculation, but ensures that the same quantities may subsequently be evaluated on \(I_\ell\).  For every coordinate \(Z) of (C3), independence of the sampled units and (C1) give
\[
 E\!\left[\left\{|I_\ell^c|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_\ell^c}(Z_i-EZ)\right\}^2\right]
 =\frac{\operatorname{Var}(Z)}{|I_\ell^c|}
 \le \frac{C}{n}.
 \tag{C7}
\]
Consequently, for every \(K>0\), applying \(P(U^2>K^2)\le E(U^2)/K^2\) coordinatewise and summing over the fixed numbers of coordinates and folds yields
\[
 \max_{1\le\ell\le L}\|\widehat\mu^{-\ell}-\mu\|
 =O_P(n^{-1/2}).
 \tag{C8}
\]
In particular, (C8) and (C2) show that all empirical denominators exceed half their population lower bounds with probability tending to one.

For each \(x_j\), the substitutions following (C3) express \(\Gamma_P(x_j)\) as a finite rational map \(F_j(\mu)\), and express \(\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x_j)\) as the same map \(F_j(\widehat\mu^{-\ell})\).  This statement includes estimation of \(q\), \(\theta\), and the correction for \(\pi_{g,1}\): each is obtained from the same finite first-moment and share vector.  By (C2), all denominators of \(F_j\) are bounded away from zero.  On a fixed neighborhood of \(\mu\), its finitely many partial derivatives are therefore bounded by a constant \(C_F\).  The coordinatewise fundamental theorem of calculus and (C8) give
\[
 \max_{\ell,j}
 \|\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x_j)-\Gamma(x_j)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le C_F\max_\ell\|\widehat\mu^{-\ell}-\mu\|
 =O_P(n^{-1/2}).
 \tag{C9}
\]
Since the support and matrix dimension are fixed,
\[
 \max_\ell\|\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}-\Gamma\|_{P_X,4,\mathrm{op}}
 =\max_\ell\left\{\sum_{j=1}^J\nu_j
 \|\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x_j)-\Gamma(x_j)\|_{\mathrm{op}}^4\right\}^{1/4}
 =O_P(n^{-1/2}).
 \tag{C10}
\]
The rate sequences \(r_{p,n}\) and \(r_{m,n}\) are nonnegative, so (C10) implies the displayed \(O_P(n^{-1/2}+r_{p,n}+r_{m,n})\) assertion.  The construction in (C3) also proves the assertion that every conditional moment in the correctly specified one-step construction is estimated by its corresponding cell average.  Applying the same ratio argument to the first moments shows that the cell propensity and regression first stages are \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\).

Set \(r_{\Gamma,n}=n^{-1/2}\) up to a fixed multiplicative constant.  Under Assumptions \(\ref{ass:fixed-contrast-rank}\) and \(\ref{ass:contrast-spectral-gap}\), if \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\) with \(0<a<1/4\), then Assumptions \(\ref{ass:rank-threshold-vanishing}\) and \(\ref{ass:rank-threshold-separation}\) hold because
\[
 \tau_n\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \frac{r_{\Gamma,n}}{\tau_n}=O(n^{-1/2+a})\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{C11}
\]
Lemma \(\ref{lem:loading-perturbation}\), applied using (C10), therefore gives consistent rank recovery and
\[
 r_{b,n}=\frac{r_{\Gamma,n}}{\tau_n}=O(n^{-1/2+a}),
 \qquad
 r_{b,n}^2+r_{\Gamma,n}^2
 =O(n^{-1+2a}+n^{-1})=o(n^{-1/2}),
 \tag{C12}
\]
where the last equality uses \(a<1/4\).

For completeness, the final continuous-covariate qualification has a generic-class certificate.  Fix one coordinate \((k,c)\), with \(k=(g,t)\), take \(X\) uniform on \([0,1]\), and make \((G,S)\) independent of \(X\) with fixed probabilities \(p^0_{a,s}\ge\varepsilon\).  Put all conditional increment means equal to zero.  In cell \((g,1)\), set only \(\Delta Y_g=\{v_\beta(X)\}^{1/2}Z\), where \(Z\) is an independent Rademacher variable; set all other increments and cells equal to zero.  Here a known partition \((B_j)_{j=1}^{m}\) divides \([0,1]\) into equal intervals and
\[
 v_\beta(x)=1+\delta\beta_j\quad\text{for }x\in B_j,
 \qquad \beta_j\in\{0,1\},\qquad 0<\delta<1.
 \tag{C13}
\]
These laws satisfy overlap and the conditional fourth-moment envelope; their conditional means are zero, so any restrictions on those means are also satisfied.  Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) gives, for the chosen diagonal coordinate,
\[
 \Gamma_{(k,c),(k,c)}(x)=\frac{v_\beta(x)}{p^0_{g,1}}.
 \tag{C14}
\]
Give the bits \(\beta_j\) independent fair Bernoulli priors.  Whatever estimator is used, at most \(n\) of the \(m\) intervals contain a sampled \(X_i\).  Conditional on the data, every bit belonging to an unvisited interval remains fair.  If the two possible values in (C14) are denoted by \(u\) and \(u+d\), where \(d=\delta/p^0_{g,1}>0\), then for every real \(a\),
\[
 \frac12\{|a-u|^4+|a-u-d|^4\}\ge\frac{d^4}{16}.
 \tag{C15}
\]
Taking \(m=2n\), integrating over a fresh \(X\), and then averaging over the bits and the sample gives, for every estimator \(\widetilde\Gamma\),
\[
 \sup_{\beta\in\{0,1\}^{2n}}
 E_\beta\!\left[
 \|\widetilde\Gamma-\Gamma_\beta\|_{P_X,4,\mathrm{op}}^4
 \right]
 \ge \left(1-\frac{n}{2n}\right)\frac{d^4}{16}
 =\frac{d^4}{32}.
 \tag{C16}
\]
Indeed, operator-norm error dominates the absolute error of the diagonal entry (C14).  Truncating that entry to \([u,u+d]\) cannot increase its loss and makes the fourth-power loss bounded; hence (C16) also rules out uniform convergence in probability.  Thus a continuous-(X\) \(L_4(P_X)\) covariance rate cannot follow from overlap and a fourth-moment envelope alone: smoothness or other structure in \(x\) is genuinely necessary.

statements.statement: Let \(\widehat r^{-\ell}(x)=\#\{j:\lambda_j(N^{\prime}\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x)N)>\tau_n\}\), and form \(\widehat H^{-\ell}\) and \(\widehat b^{-\ell}\) from the retained eigencomponents. Under fixed rank, separated positive spectrum, \(L_4(P_X)\) covariance error, and \(r_{\Gamma,n}=o(\tau_n)\), \(P_X\{\widehat r^{-\ell}(X)\ne r_0\}=O_P\{(r_{\Gamma,n}/\tau_n)^4\}\) uniformly over folds. The thresholded Moore--Penrose perturbation and its projector obey \[\max_{\ell}\|\widehat b^{-\ell}-b^{\star}\|_{P_X,2}+\max_{\ell}\|\widehat b^{-\ell}-b^{\star}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(r_{b,n})=o_P(1),\qquad r_{b,n}=r_{\Gamma,n}/\tau_n.\] On the consistently selected spectral range the sharper local bound is \(O_P(r_{\Gamma,n})\). Thus both rank recovery and the loading rate are derived from covariance learning and threshold separation rather than supplied by an oracle rank or a standalone loading assumption.
statements.justification: The learned loading rate must follow from covariance estimation and stable quotient geometry rather than being assumed as an independent first-stage property.
statements.gap: Standard Moore--Penrose perturbation bounds do not by themselves control the DDD loading in \(L_4(P_X)\); the conditional moment envelope and the affine fixed-rank construction close that step.
statements.consumer: The result supplies the loading remainder bound used by both the efficient estimator and the efficiency-gap estimator.
statements.proof_tex:
For a fold \(\ell\), write
\[
 \widetilde H_\ell(x)=N'\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x)N,
 \qquad
 E_\ell(x)=\|\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x)-\Gamma(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
 \tag{B1}
\]
Because \(N'N=I\),
\[
 \|\widetilde H_\ell(x)-H(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le E_\ell(x).
 \tag{B2}
\]
For every unit vector \(v\), the absolute difference between the Rayleigh quotients of \(\widetilde H_\ell(x)\) and \(H(x)\) is at most \(E_\ell(x)\).  Taking the successive minima and maxima in the variational characterization of the ordered eigenvalues therefore gives
\[
 \max_j|\lambda_j\{\widetilde H_\ell(x)\}-\lambda_j\{H(x)\}|
 \le E_\ell(x).
 \tag{B3}
\]
By Assumptions \(\ref{ass:rank-threshold-vanishing}\) and \(\ref{ass:contrast-spectral-gap}\), \(\tau_n<\kappa/2\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Assumptions \(\ref{ass:fixed-contrast-rank}\) and \(\ref{ass:contrast-spectral-gap}\) say that \(H(x)\) has exactly \(r_0\) eigenvalues in \([\kappa,\kappa^{-1}]\) and all its other eigenvalues are zero, for almost every \(x\).  Hence (B3) shows that
\[
 \{\widehat r^{-\ell}(x)\ne r_0\}\subseteq\{E_\ell(x)>\tau_n\}.
 \tag{B4}
\]
Indeed, a retained eigenvalue from the zero cluster requires \(E_\ell(x)>\tau_n\), whereas failure to retain a positive population eigenvalue requires \(E_\ell(x)\ge\kappa-\tau_n>\tau_n\).  Conditional on the training sample, the elementary bound \(P_X(U>t)\le t^{-4}E_X(U^4)\), Assumption \(\ref{ass:covariance-rate}\), and fixed \(L\) now yield
\[
 \max_{1\le\ell\le L}P_X\{\widehat r^{-\ell}(X)\ne r_0\}
 \le \tau_n^{-4}\max_\ell\|\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}-\Gamma\|_{P_X,4,\mathrm{op}}^4
 =O_P\!\left\{\left(\frac{r_{\Gamma,n}}{\tau_n}\right)^4\right\}.
 \tag{B5}
\]
This proves the rank statement, including its uniformity over the fixed folds.

It remains to control the loading.  By Lemma \(\ref{lem:singular-operator}\), with
\[
 g(x)=N'\Gamma(x)b^0,
 \qquad
 z^0(x)=H(x)^\dagger g(x),
 \tag{B6}
\]
one has \(g(x)\in\operatorname{range}H(x)\), \(H(x)z^0(x)=g(x)\), and
\[
 b^\star(x)=b^0-Nz^0(x).
 \tag{B7}
\]
The moment conditions invoked here also make the constants below uniform in \(x\).  In fact, Assumption \(\ref{ass:cell-overlap}\) implies \(\pi_{g,1}\ge\varepsilon\) and bounds every propensity ratio in Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\).  Assumption \(\ref{ass:conditional-fourth-envelope}\), the fixed horizon, and \(|z_1+\cdots+z_d|^4\le d^3\sum_h|z_h|^4\) then give
\[
 \operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{x}E\{\|\Psi_P(O)\|^4\mid X=x\}<\infty.
 \tag{B8}
\]
Thus \(\sup_x\|\Gamma(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\infty\).  Since every positive eigenvalue of \(H(x)\) is at least \(\kappa\), (B6) implies
\[
 \operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{x}\|z^0(x)\|
 \le \kappa^{-1}\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{x}\|N'\Gamma(x)b^0\|<\infty;
 \tag{B9}
\]
the inequality is also valid under the zero-rank convention, when \(z^0=0\).

Let \(\widetilde H_{\ell,\tau}(x)\) retain exactly the eigencomponents of \(\widetilde H_\ell(x)\) whose eigenvalues exceed \(\tau_n\), and put
\[
 \widehat P_{\ell,\tau}(x)
 =\widetilde H_{\ell,\tau}(x)^\dagger\widetilde H_\ell(x),
 \qquad
 P_H(x)=H(x)^\dagger H(x),
 \qquad
 \widehat g_\ell(x)=N'\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x)b^0.
 \tag{B10}
\]
These are the orthogonal projectors onto the retained empirical space and \(\operatorname{range}H(x)\), respectively.  Spectral truncation gives
\[
 \|\widetilde H_{\ell,\tau}(x)^\dagger\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le\tau_n^{-1},
 \qquad
 \|\widehat g_\ell(x)-g(x)\|
 \le \|b^0\|E_\ell(x).
 \tag{B11}
\]
Using \(g=Hz^0\) and the fact that the truncated inverse annihilates the discarded empirical eigenvectors gives the exact identity
\[
 \widetilde H_{\ell,\tau}^\dagger\widehat g_\ell
 =\widehat P_{\ell,\tau}z^0
 +\widetilde H_{\ell,\tau}^\dagger
 \{(H-\widetilde H_\ell)z^0+(\widehat g_\ell-g)\}.
 \tag{B12}
\]

We next bound the projector term without assuming rank recovery.  If \(E_\ell(x)\le\tau_n\), (B3) and \(\tau_n<\kappa/2\) show that the retained empirical space has dimension \(r_0\).  If \(\widehat u\) is a unit retained empirical eigenvector with eigenvalue \(\widehat\lambda\), then \(\widehat\lambda\ge\kappa-E_\ell(x)\).  Multiplying
\(\widetilde H_\ell\widehat u=\widehat\lambda\widehat u\)
by \(I-P_H\), using \((I-P_H)H=0\), and applying (B2) yields
\[
 \|(I-P_H)\widehat u\|
 \le\frac{E_\ell(x)}{\kappa-E_\ell(x)}.
 \tag{B13}
\]
 Applying this bound to an orthonormal basis of the retained space, using equality of the two ranks, and bounding the operator norm by the Frobenius norm bounds both off-diagonal blocks of the two projectors; in particular,
\[
 \|\widehat P_{\ell,\tau}(x)-P_H(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le\frac{2\sqrt{r_0}\,E_\ell(x)}{\kappa-E_\ell(x)}.
\tag{B14}
\]
If \(E_\ell(x)>\tau_n\), the difference of two orthogonal projectors has norm at most two, and hence at most \(2E_\ell(x)/\tau_n\).  Combining the two cases, using \(P_Hz^0=z^0\), (B9), (B11), and (B12), gives a fixed constant \(C\) such that
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \|\widehat b^{-\ell}(x)-b^\star(x)\|
 &=\|N\{\widetilde H_{\ell,\tau}(x)^\dagger\widehat g_\ell(x)-z^0(x)\}\|\\
 &\le C\frac{E_\ell(x)}{\tau_n}
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{B15}
\]
for almost every \(x\) and all sufficiently large \(n\).  Assumption \(\ref{ass:covariance-rate}\) therefore implies
\[
 \max_\ell\|\widehat b^{-\ell}-b^\star\|_{P_X,4}
 \le C\tau_n^{-1}max_\ell\|\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}-\Gamma\|_{P_X,4,\mathrm{op}}
 =O_P\!\left(\frac{r_{\Gamma,n}}{\tau_n}\right).
 \tag{B16}
\]
Because \(P_X\) is a probability measure, \(\|f\|_{P_X,2}\le\|f\|_{P_X,4}\), so the same rate holds in \(L_2(P_X)\).  By the definition of \(r_{b,n}\) and Assumption \(\ref{ass:rank-threshold-separation}\), (B16) is \(O_P(r_{b,n})=o_P(1)\).

Finally, the sharper assertion concerns the consistently selected spectral region
\[
 \mathcal A_{\ell n}=\{x:E_\ell(x)\le\tau_n\}.
 \tag{B17}
\]
On this region, (B3) selects exactly the population positive cluster, its retained eigenvalues are at least \(\kappa-\tau_n\ge\kappa/2\), and (B11) improves to \(\|\widetilde H_{\ell,\tau}^\dagger\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2/\kappa\).  Equations (B12)--(B14) then give
\[
 \max_\ell
 \|\mathbf 1_{\mathcal A_{\ell n}}(\widehat b^{-\ell}-b^\star)\|_{P_X,4}
 \le C\max_\ell\|\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}-\Gamma\|_{P_X,4,\mathrm{op}}
 =O_P(r_{\Gamma,n}),
 \tag{B18}
\]
which is the claimed sharper local bound on the consistently selected spectral range.

statements.statement:
Suppose \(P\) is a fixed conditional-mean interior law induced by the global OVS model, \(X\) has fixed finite support with every support mass bounded below, and every first stage in Definition \(\ref{def:crossfit-estimator}\) is its corresponding training-cell average.  Under independent fixed-\(T\) sampling, global retained-cell overlap, the global conditional fourth-moment envelope, fixed-fold cross-fitting, the threshold condition, and \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}>0\), take \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\) for \(0<a<1/4\).  Then
\[
\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}-\tau_\omega(P)\}
=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(O_i)+o_P(1)
\ \Rightarrow\ N(0,V_{\mathrm{OVS}}),
\tag{41}
\]
\[
\widehat V_{\mathrm{eff}}\longrightarrow_P V_{\mathrm{OVS}},
\qquad
P\{\tau_\omega(P)\in\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha}\}\longrightarrow1-\alpha.
\tag{42}
\]
Thus the OVS-complete-normal estimator attains the pointwise semiparametric efficiency bound of the published class.  The local complete-normal correction remains regular on the published subclass but need not attain its smaller bound.  No continuous-covariate, rank-uniform, or equality-boundary inference claim is made.
statements.justification: The exhaustive augmented OVS signal converts the published population projection into an attainable pointwise estimator on fixed finite support.
statements.gap: The proof deliberately excludes continuous covariates and rank-uniform sequences.
statements.consumer: A CRAN \(\texttt{triplediff}\) optional backend can implement this verified discrete-covariate branch and its Wald interval.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(\eta=(p,m)\), and define the population projection coefficient and uncentered reference score by
\[
\alpha_P(x)=K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x)^\dagger r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x),
\qquad
\mu_P(O)=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\omega_k R_{k,c_0(k),P}(O).
\tag{41a}
\]
Theorem \(\ref{thm:observable-equivalence}\) gives every published observable equality, and Lemma \(\ref{lem:ovs-orthogonal-normal-signal}\) therefore gives
\[
S^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O;\eta)=Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O),
\qquad E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\mid X]=0.
\tag{41b}
\]
The fixed support-mass lower bound, retained-cell overlap, independent fixed-\(T\) sampling, and the conditional fourth-moment envelope give the root-\(n\) finite-cell rates derived in Proposition \(\ref{prop:ovs-normal-finite-support-rates}\).  With \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\), \(0<a<1/4\), that proposition also gives, uniformly over the fixed number of folds,
\[
\|\widehat\alpha_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}-\alpha_P\|_{P_X,4}
=O_P(n^{-1/2+a})=o_P(1).
\tag{41c}
\]

We first expand the cross-fitted ratio part.  For \(k=(g,t)\), put
\[
M_{a,s,k}(x)=\sum_{u=g}^t m_{a,s,u}(x),
\qquad
\widehat M_{a,s,k}^{-\ell}(x)=\sum_{u=g}^t\widehat m_{a,s,u}^{-\ell}(x),
\]
and let \(B_{k,c,P}\) denote the bracketed numerator in Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\), so \(R_{k,c,P}=B_{k,c,P}/\pi_{g,1}\).  Conditional on the training complement, direct addition and subtraction of the true regressions in the estimated bracket gives the exact identity
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_P[\widehat B_{k,c}^{-\ell}-B_{k,c,P}\mid X,\mathcal D_{-\ell}]
={}&\left(\frac{\widehat p_{g,1}^{-\ell}p_{g,0}}{\widehat p_{g,0}^{-\ell}}-p_{g,1}\right)
(\widehat M_{g,0,k}^{-\ell}-M_{g,0,k})\\
&+\left(\frac{\widehat p_{g,1}^{-\ell}p_{c,1}}{\widehat p_{c,1}^{-\ell}}-p_{g,1}\right)
(\widehat M_{c,1,k}^{-\ell}-M_{c,1,k})\\
&+\left(p_{g,1}-\frac{\widehat p_{g,1}^{-\ell}p_{c,0}}{\widehat p_{c,0}^{-\ell}}\right)
(\widehat M_{c,0,k}^{-\ell}-M_{c,0,k}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{41d}
\]
There is no \((g,1)\) regression-error term because the plug-in conditional contrast and the treated-cell residual in the first bracket cancel it algebraically.  Clipping and overlap make each coefficient in parentheses Lipschitz in \(\widehat p^{-\ell}-p\).  The finite-cell root-\(n\) rates and H\"older's inequality consequently imply
\[
\|E_P[\widehat B_{k,c}^{-\ell}-B_{k,c,P}\mid X,\mathcal D_{-\ell}]\|_{P_X,2}
=O_P(n^{-1}),
\qquad
\|\widehat B_{k,c}^{-\ell}-B_{k,c,P}\|_{P,2}=O_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{41e}
\]
The second bound follows by expanding the displayed score formula: every coefficient error is root-\(n\), all inverse propensities are bounded, and every residual has a bounded conditional second moment by the conditional fourth-moment envelope.

By fixed-fold cross-fitting, conditional on \(\mathcal D_{-\ell}\) the validation observations in \(I_\ell\) are independent of the estimated functions used there.  Conditional Chebyshev inequality applied to the centered difference in (41e), followed by summation over the fixed number of folds, yields
\[
\frac1n\sum_{\ell=1}^L\sum_{i\in I_\ell}
\widehat B_{i,k,c}^{-\ell}
=P B_{k,c,P}+(\mathbb P_n-P)B_{k,c,P}+o_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{41f}
\]
Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) gives \(P B_{k,c,P}=\pi_{g,1}\theta_k(P)\).  Also, retained-cell overlap implies \(\pi_{g,1}>0\), while independent sampling and finite variance give \(\widehat\pi_{g,1}-\pi_{g,1}=O_P(n^{-1/2})\).  The exact scalar expansion
\[
\widehat\pi_{g,1}^{-1}-\pi_{g,1}^{-1}
=-\pi_{g,1}^{-2}(\widehat\pi_{g,1}-\pi_{g,1})
+\frac{(\widehat\pi_{g,1}-\pi_{g,1})^2}
{\pi_{g,1}^2\widehat\pi_{g,1}}
\tag{41g}
\]
has an \(O_P(n^{-1})\) remainder.  Combining (41f)--(41g), and using
\(\widehat\pi_{g,1}-\pi_{g,1}=(\mathbb P_n-P)\mathbf 1\{G=g,S=1\}\), proves
\[
\frac{n^{-1}\sum_{\ell}\sum_{i\in I_\ell}\widehat B_{i,k,c}^{-\ell}}
{\widehat\pi_{g,1}}-\theta_k(P)
=(\mathbb P_n-P)\left\{
R_{k,c,P}-\frac{\theta_k(P)}{\pi_{g,1}}\mathbf 1\{G=g,S=1\}
\right\}+o_P(n^{-1/2})
=(\mathbb P_n-P)\Psi_{k,c,P}+o_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{41h}
\]
Thus the global empirical share contributes exactly the denominator-derivative term in the corrected score; it is not absorbed into an uncorrected centering.

We next expand the complete-normal correction.  Lemma \(\ref{lem:ovs-orthogonal-normal-signal}\), the root-\(n\) cell rates, and (41b) imply
\[
\|E_P[\widehat S^{\mathrm{OVS},-\ell}\mid X,\mathcal D_{-\ell}]\|_{P_X,2}
=O_P(n^{-1}),
\qquad
\|\widehat S^{\mathrm{OVS},-\ell}-Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\|_{P,2}=O_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{41i}
\]
The finite-support population coefficient \(\alpha_P\) is finite at every support point under the Moore--Penrose convention.  Equations (41c), (41i), H\"older's inequality, and the conditional fourth-moment envelope therefore give
\[
\|\widehat\alpha_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}(X)'
\widehat S^{\mathrm{OVS},-\ell}
-\alpha_P(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\|_{P,2}=o_P(1).
\tag{41j}
\]
Moreover, (41i) and \(\widehat\alpha_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}=O_P(1)\) make the conditional expectation of the first product in (41j) \(O_P(n^{-1})\), whereas the expectation of the second product is zero by (41b).  Cross-fit independence and conditional Chebyshev inequality now show
\[
\frac1n\sum_{\ell=1}^L\sum_{i\in I_\ell}
\widehat\alpha_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}(X_i)'
\widehat S_i^{\mathrm{OVS},-\ell}
=\mathbb P_n\{\alpha_P(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\}+o_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{41k}
\]

Summing (41h) at \(c=c_0(k)\) with the fixed weights \(\omega_k\), and subtracting (41k), proves
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}-\tau_\omega(P)\}
&=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n
\left\{\psi_P^0(O_i)-\alpha_P(X_i)'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O_i)\right\}+o_P(1)\\
&=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(O_i)+o_P(1),
\end{aligned}
\tag{41l}
\]
where the second equality is Definition \(\ref{def:ovs-normal-projection}\).  The summands are independent and identically distributed by the sampling assumption, have mean zero by (41b) and the ambient-gradient centering, and are square integrable by overlap and the fourth-moment condition.  Their variance is \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}>0\) by the theorem's positivity hypothesis.  Lemma \(\ref{lem:iid-central-limit}\) applied to (41l) proves (41).

For variance consistency, let \(\widehat\phi_i\) be the displayed quantity in Definition \(\ref{def:crossfit-estimator}\), and let \(\phi_i=\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(O_i)\).  Equations (37c), (41c), (41i), the ratio expansion (41g), and \(\widehat\theta_k-\theta_k=O_P(n^{-1/2})\), which follows from (41h), imply foldwise
\[
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n(\widehat\phi_i-\phi_i)^2=o_P(1).
\tag{42a}
\]
To see this without an empirical-process assumption, condition one fold at a time on its training complement, apply Markov's inequality to the nonnegative squared difference using its \(o_P(1)\) conditional mean, and sum over the fixed number of folds; the global shares and preliminary ratios are finite-dimensional root-\(n\) terms and hence do not alter the conclusion.  By Cauchy--Schwarz, (42a) gives
\[
\left|\mathbb P_n\widehat\phi^2-\mathbb P_n\phi^2\right|
\le \{\mathbb P_n(\widehat\phi-\phi)^2\}^{1/2}
\{2\mathbb P_n\phi^2+2\mathbb P_n(\widehat\phi-\phi)^2\}^{1/2}
=o_P(1).
\tag{42b}
\]
The ordinary law of large numbers applies to \(\phi_i^2\), which is integrable, and gives \(\mathbb P_n\phi^2\to_P V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\).  Also \(|\mathbb P_n\widehat\phi-\mathbb P_n\phi|\le\{\mathbb P_n(\widehat\phi-\phi)^2\}^{1/2}=o_P(1)\), while \(\mathbb P_n\phi=o_P(1)\).  Expanding the centered empirical second moment in Definition \(\ref{def:crossfit-estimator}\) therefore proves
\[
\widehat V_{\mathrm{eff}}\longrightarrow_P V_{\mathrm{OVS}}.
\tag{42c}
\]
Because \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}>0\), (42c) makes the estimated standard deviation divided by \(\sqrt{V_{\mathrm{OVS}}}\) converge to one.  Combining this fact with (41), and sandwiching the studentized statistic between Gaussian continuity points, yields
\[
P\{\tau_\omega(P)\in\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha}\}\longrightarrow1-\alpha.
\]
Finally, Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\), whose finite-support and conditional-mean-interior hypotheses are imposed here, identifies \(\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\) as the canonical gradient in the published OVS observed-law tangent space and \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\) as its pointwise efficiency bound.  Hence the explicit cross-fitted estimator attains that bound at the fixed law.  The same theorem and Theorem \(\ref{thm:observable-equivalence}\) give \(\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}\subseteq\mathcal T_P\), so the localized canonical gradient \(\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}\), which represents the derivative on \(\mathcal T_P\), also represents it on every published score and is therefore a valid regular gradient on the published subclass.  Its variance satisfies
\[
V_{\mathrm{can}}-V_{\mathrm{OVS}}
=E_P[(\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}-\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P})^2],
\]
again by Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\).  Thus a regular estimator with the localized influence function attains the published bound exactly when the displayed squared distance vanishes, equivalently when the conditional published-normal equation in that theorem holds; otherwise its variance is strictly larger.  Every step used fixed support and a fixed-law positive spectrum after threshold recovery; none establishes continuous-covariate, rank-uniform, or equality-boundary inference.

statements.statement:
For either \(b^{\mathrm{cmp}}\in\{b^{\mathrm{OVS}},b^{\mathrm{const}}\}\),
\[
\operatorname{Var}_P\{b^{\mathrm{cmp}\prime}\Psi_P(O)\}-V_{\mathrm{agg}}
=E_P[(b^{\mathrm{cmp}}-b^\star(X))'\Gamma_P(X)(b^{\mathrm{cmp}}-b^\star(X))].
\tag{E1}
\]
Its losses relative to the localized and published bounds are, respectively,
\[
\operatorname{Var}_P\{b^{\mathrm{cmp}\prime}\Psi_P(O)\}-V_{\mathrm{can}}
=E_P[(b^{\mathrm{cmp}}-b^\star)'\Gamma_P(b^{\mathrm{cmp}}-b^\star)]
+\Delta_{\mathrm{normal}}(P),
\tag{E2}
\]
\[
\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}(P)
=\operatorname{Var}_P\{b^{\mathrm{cmp}\prime}\Psi_P(O)\}-V_{\mathrm{OVS}}
=E_P[(b^{\mathrm{cmp}}-b^\star)'\Gamma_P(b^{\mathrm{cmp}}-b^\star)]
+\Delta_{\mathrm{normal}}(P)+\Delta_{\mathrm{model}}(P).
\tag{E3}
\]
Equality with the aggregate score-family optimum holds if and only if
\[
N'\Gamma_P(X)b^{\mathrm{cmp}}=0
\quad P_X\text{-almost surely}.
\tag{E4}
\]
Equality with the localized-model bound holds if and only if
\[
E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\{b^{\mathrm{cmp}\prime}\Psi_P\}\mid X]=0
\quad P_X\text{-almost surely},
\tag{E5}
\]
and equality with the published OVS bound holds if and only if
\[
E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\{b^{\mathrm{cmp}\prime}\Psi_P\}\mid X]=0
\quad P_X\text{-almost surely}.
\tag{E6}
\]
Thus the three residuals in Definition \(\ref{def:projection-diagnostic}\) answer three distinct projection questions.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix one of the two declared comparators and abbreviate \(b=b^{\mathrm{cmp}}\).  First note from Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) that the cell-residual terms have conditional mean zero.  Hence, for \((k,c)\in\mathcal I\), with \(k=(g,t)\),
\[
 E_P[\Psi_{k,c,P}(O)\mid X]
 =\frac{p_{g,1}(X)}{\pi_{g,1}}\{q_{k,c}(X)-\theta_k(P)\}
 =h_k(X).
\tag{E7}
\]
The last equality uses the observable clean-comparison equality, under which \(q_{k,c}=q_{k,c_0(k)}\).  Both \(b\) and \(b^\star(X)\) are feasible, so \(A'b=A'b^\star(X)=\omega\).  It follows from (E7) that
\[
 E_P[b'\Psi_P\mid X]=E_P[b^\star(X)'\Psi_P\mid X]=\omega'h(X).
\tag{E8}
\]
The definition of \(\theta_k(P)\) also gives \(E_P[h_k(X)]=0\), so both scores in (E8) are mean zero.
Consequently the conditional-variance identity and the definition of \(\Gamma\) give
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_P(b'\Psi_P)-\operatorname{Var}_P(b^{\star\prime}\Psi_P)
 =E_P[b'\Gamma_P(X)b-b^{\star\prime}\Gamma_P(X)b^\star].
\tag{E9}
\]

Because the columns of \(N\) are an orthonormal basis of \(\ker(A')\), there is a measurable vector \(z(X)\) such that
\[
 d(X):=b-b^\star(X)=Nz(X).
\tag{E10}
\]
Lemma \(\ref{lem:singular-operator}\) gives \(N'\Gamma_P(X)b^\star(X)=0\).  Expanding the integrand in (E9) therefore yields, pointwise,
\[
 b'\Gamma b-b^{\star\prime}\Gamma b^\star
 =2d'\Gamma b^\star+d'\Gamma d
 =z'H z
 =(b-b^\star)'\Gamma(b-b^\star).
\tag{E11}
\]
Since \(V_{\mathrm{agg}}=\operatorname{Var}_P(b^{\star\prime}\Psi_P)\), integration of (E11) proves (E1).  Adding the defining identities
\[
 V_{\mathrm{agg}}-V_{\mathrm{can}}=\Delta_{\mathrm{normal}}(P),
 \qquad
 V_{\mathrm{can}}-V_{\mathrm{OVS}}=\Delta_{\mathrm{model}}(P)
\tag{E12}
\]
proves (E2) and (E3).

For the first equality characterization, again use (E10) and Lemma \(\ref{lem:singular-operator}\) to obtain
\[
 N'\Gamma_P(X)b
 =N'\Gamma_P(X)\{b-b^\star(X)\}
 =H(X)z(X).
\tag{E13}
\]
If (E13) vanishes, the integrand \(z'Hz\) in (E11) vanishes.  Conversely, equality in (E1) implies \(E_P[z'Hz]=0\).  The integrand is nonnegative because \(H=N'\Gamma N\) is positive semidefinite, so \(z'H z=0\) almost surely.  For a positive semidefinite matrix, \(z'Hz=\|H^{1/2}z\|^2=0\) implies \(Hz=0\); (E13) then vanishes.  This proves (E4), including singular cases.

It remains to distinguish the two model-normal equations.  Let \(\mathscr S_{\mathrm{per}}\) and \(\mathscr S_{\mathrm{OVS}}\) denote the closed measurable spans generated by \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\) and \(Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\), respectively.  If \(b^{\mathrm{ref}}\) puts weight \(\omega_k\) on \((k,c_0(k))\) and zero on the other coordinates, then \(A'b^{\mathrm{ref}}=\omega\) and \(\psi_P^0=b^{\mathrm{ref}\prime}\Psi_P\).  Thus \(b-b^{\mathrm{ref}}\in\ker(A')\).  Within a target block, the denominator-correction terms cancel, so
\[
 (b-b^{\mathrm{ref}})'\Psi_P=(b-b^{\mathrm{ref}})'R_P\in\mathcal C_P.
\tag{E14}
\]
For a single comparison replacement, direct subtraction in Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) gives
\[
 \Psi_{k,c,P}-\Psi_{k,c_0(k),P}
 =-\frac{p_{g,1}(X)}{\pi_{g,1}}
   \sum_{u=g}^{t} Z_{(u,c,c_0(k)),P}.
\tag{E15}
\]
Every formal row on the right of (E15) is in the row span defining \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{per}}\).  Moreover, both \(c\) and \(c_0(k)\) exceed \(t\ge u\), so each such row is also an OVS row.  Linear decomposition within each target block, followed by closure, therefore proves
\[
 \mathcal C_P\subseteq\mathscr S_{\mathrm{per}}
 \subseteq\mathscr S_{\mathrm{OVS}}.
\tag{E16}
\]

We next verify the projection formulas, including singular cases.  For either normal vector \(Z\), write
\[
 K(X)=E_P[ZZ'\mid X],\qquad r(X)=E_P[Z\psi_P^0\mid X].
\]
If \(v\in\ker K(X)\), then
\[
 E_P[(v'Z)^2\mid X]=v'K(X)v=0,
\]
and hence \(v'Z=0\) conditionally almost surely and \(v'r(X)=0\).  Thus \(r(X)\in\operatorname{range}K(X)\), and
\[
 E_P\!\left[Z\{\psi_P^0-r(X)'K(X)^\dagger Z\}\mid X\right]
 =r(X)-K(X)K(X)^\dagger r(X)=0.
\tag{E17}
\]
