Moreover, with \(\alpha=K^\dagger r\), expansion of the nonnegative conditional square \(E_P[(\psi_P^0-\alpha'Z)^2\mid X]\) shows that \(r'K^\dagger r\le E_P[(\psi_P^0)^2\mid X]\); hence the displayed projection is square-integrable.  Equation (E17), first for bounded measurable multipliers and then for their \(L_2(P)\) closure, proves that \(r'K^\dagger Z\) is the orthogonal projection of \(\psi_P^0\) onto the corresponding normal span.  Therefore \(\phi_{\mathrm{can}}\) is orthogonal to \(\mathscr S_{\mathrm{per}}\), and \(\phi_{\mathrm{OVS}}\) is orthogonal to \(\mathscr S_{\mathrm{OVS}}\).  In the fixed-finite-support conditional-mean-interior regime, Theorem \(\ref{thm:observable-equivalence}\) identifies these spans with the respective tangent orthocomplements, and Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\) identifies the residuals with the corresponding canonical gradients.

Put \(g=b'\Psi_P\).  By (E14)--(E16), \(g-\psi_P^0\) belongs to each relevant normal span.  Orthogonal decomposition using (E17) consequently gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_P(g)-V_{\mathrm{can}}
 =\|g-\phi_{\mathrm{can}}\|_{L_2(P)}^2,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P(g)-V_{\mathrm{OVS}}
 =\|g-\phi_{\mathrm{OVS}}\|_{L_2(P)}^2.
\tag{E18}
\]
The first difference in (E18) is zero exactly when \(g\perp\mathscr S_{\mathrm{per}}\), and the second is zero exactly when \(g\perp\mathscr S_{\mathrm{OVS}}\).  For a finite-dimensional conditional normal vector, orthogonality to every square-integrable measurable multiple of \(Z\) is equivalent to
\[
 E_P[Zg\mid X]=0
\quad P_X\text{-almost surely};
\tag{E19}
\]
the forward implication follows by the defining property of conditional expectation, and the reverse implication follows by testing against bounded measurable multipliers and truncating.  Applying (E19) to the two normal vectors proves (E5) and (E6).  Together with (E4), these are precisely the three residuals reported in Definition \(\ref{def:projection-diagnostic}\).
statements.justification: Three observable residuals distinguish aggregate optimality, localized-model efficiency, and published OVS efficiency.
statements.gap: Neither the aggregate KKT equation nor the localized normal equation alone certifies equality with the published bound.
statements.consumer: The optional \(\texttt{triplediff}\) backend can report all three diagnostics without conflating their meanings.

statements.statement:
For every \(0<r<\sqrt 7/3\), \(0<|\delta|<1/8\), and \(\omega=(\omega_1,\omega_2)'\) with \(\omega_2\ne0\), the law \(Q^{\mathrm{bin}}_{r,\delta}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M\), and its outcomes satisfy \(\max_{t\in\mathcal T}|Y_t|<3/8\) almost surely. In score order \(((2,2),3),((2,2),\infty),((2,3),\infty)\),
\[
\Gamma(x)=\frac{3}{16}
\begin{pmatrix}
2&1&1\\
1&2&2+xr\\
1&2+xr&4+2xr
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Its leading principal minors before multiplication by \(3/16\) are \(2\), \(3\), and \(6-2r^2\); hence \(\Gamma(x)\) is positive definite for both \(x\in\{-1,1\}\), and its conditional eigenvalues are separated from zero at every fixed \(r\) in the displayed range. Every feasible loading has the form
\[
b(q)=\bigl(\omega_1/2+q,\ \omega_1/2-q,\ \omega_2\bigr)',
\]
and the conditional optimum is
\[
q^\star(x)=\frac{(1+xr)\omega_2}{2},
\qquad
b^\star(x)=b\{q^\star(x)\}.
\]
The best joint constant and published componentwise loadings are distinct:
\[
b^{\mathrm{const}}=b(\omega_2/2),
\qquad
b^{\mathrm{OVS}}=b(0).
\]
For every deterministic \(q\), the loss relative to the published OVS bound is
\[
\Delta\{b(q)\}
=\frac{3}{8}\left(q-\frac{\omega_2}{2}\right)^2
+\frac{3r^2\omega_2^2}{32}.
\]
Consequently
\[
\Delta(b^{\mathrm{const}})=\frac{3r^2\omega_2^2}{32}>0,
\qquad
\Delta(b^{\mathrm{OVS}})=\frac{3(1+r^2)\omega_2^2}{32}>0.
\]
In this architecture the deterministic row conventions give
\[
Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}=Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}=Z_{2;3,\infty},
\qquad
\mathcal C_P=\mathcal T_P^\perp=\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp.
\]
Thus \(\Delta_{\mathrm{normal}}=\Delta_{\mathrm{model}}=0\), so all displayed losses are genuinely relative to \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\). At \(r=\omega_2=1/2\), the minimum loss over all deterministic feasible loadings, attained by \(b^{\mathrm{const}}\), is \(3/512\), whereas the loss of \(b^{\mathrm{OVS}}\) is \(15/512\).
statements.justification: The corrected cumulative-level witness proves equality of the aggregate, localized, and published normal closures before interpreting either comparator's loss.
statements.gap: The joint constant and componentwise OVS loadings differ: their benchmark published-bound losses are \(3/512\) and \(15/512\), respectively.
statements.consumer: The witness supplies deterministic covariance, loading, tangent-normal, and comparator-gap regression tests for the optional backend.
statements.proof_tex:
The construction gives
\[
 p_{a,s}(x)=\frac16
 \quad\text{for every }a\in\{2,3,\infty\},\ s\in\{0,1\},\ x\in\{-1,1\},
 \qquad \pi_{2,1}=\frac16.
\tag{Q1}
\]
Because \(|(U^{\mathrm w}+V^{\mathrm w})/8|\le 1/4\) and \(|\delta|<1/8\),
\[
 \max_{t\in\mathcal T}|Y_t|
 \le \frac14+|\delta|<\frac38.
\tag{Q2}
\]
Consistency holds by the last clause of Definition \(\ref{def:binary-witness}\).  If \(s=0\), the treatment term in that definition is zero at every date, proving no effect on ineligible units.  If \(u<a\), then \(Y_u(a,1)=Y_u(\infty,1)=Z_u^{\mathrm w}\), proving no anticipation.  Conditional on \((G,X)\), the law of \((U^{\mathrm w},V^{\mathrm w})\) does not depend on \(S\).  Therefore every untreated within-cohort eligibility gap is zero, so both sides of every global conditional parallel-gap restriction in Definition \(\ref{def:target-model}\) are zero.  Hence \(Q^{\mathrm{bin}}_{r,\delta}\in\mathcal M\).

Since \(r<\sqrt7/3<1\), each conditional sign probability \(\{1+\rho_a(x)uv\}/4\) is strictly positive.  In every cohort--eligibility cell the conditional support of \((\Delta Y_2,\Delta Y_3)\) is therefore the four vertices of a translated square.  Both signs have conditional mean zero, so the conditional mean is the translated center, which is in the relative interior of that square.  Thus the induced observed law is conditional-mean interior.  Equation (Q1) supplies overlap, (Q2) supplies the fourth-moment condition, and the two values of \(X\) have positive probability.

The observed increments are
\[
 \Delta Y_2=\frac{U^{\mathrm w}}8+\delta S\mathbf 1\{G=2\},
 \qquad
 \Delta Y_3=\frac{V^{\mathrm w}}8+\delta S\mathbf 1\{G=3\}.
\tag{Q3}
\]
Substitution of their cell means into the definition of \(q\) shows that all three retained conditional DDD contrasts equal \(\delta\).  The two target effects also equal \(\delta\), and therefore
\[
 q_{k,c}(X)-\theta_k(P)=0
 \quad\text{for every }(k,c)\in\mathcal I.
\tag{Q4}
\]
Put \(a=3/4\).  Every propensity ratio in Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) equals one, and \(1/\pi_{2,1}=6\).  Substituting (Q3)--(Q4) into that definition gives the following complete conditional score table, in the coordinate order stated in the theorem:
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
(G,S)&\Psi_{(2,2),3}&\Psi_{(2,2),\infty}&\Psi_{(2,3),\infty}\\ \hline
(2,1)&aU^{\mathrm w}&aU^{\mathrm w}&a(U^{\mathrm w}+V^{\mathrm w})\\
(2,0)&-aU^{\mathrm w}&-aU^{\mathrm w}&-a(U^{\mathrm w}+V^{\mathrm w})\\
(3,1)&-aU^{\mathrm w}&0&0\\
(3,0)&aU^{\mathrm w}&0&0\\
(\infty,1)&0&-aU^{\mathrm w}&-a(U^{\mathrm w}+V^{\mathrm w})\\
(\infty,0)&0&aU^{\mathrm w}&a(U^{\mathrm w}+V^{\mathrm w}).
\end{array}
\tag{Q5}
\]
Each row has conditional probability \(1/6\).  From the sign law,
\[
 E_P[U^{\mathrm w}V^{\mathrm w}\mid X=x,G=2]
 =E_P[U^{\mathrm w}V^{\mathrm w}\mid X=x,G=3]=0,
 \qquad
 E_P[U^{\mathrm w}V^{\mathrm w}\mid X=x,G=\infty]=xr.
\tag{Q6}
\]
Every column of (Q5) has conditional mean zero.  Multiplying the six rows coordinatewise, using \(E[(U^{\mathrm w})^2]=E[(V^{\mathrm w})^2]=1\) and (Q6), yields
\[
 \Gamma(x)=\frac{3}{16}
 \begin{pmatrix}
 2&1&1\\
 1&2&2+xr\\
 1&2+xr&4+2xr
 \end{pmatrix}.
\tag{Q7}
\]
For example, its second--third entry is the sum of \(3/16\) from the cohort-two cells and \(3(1+xr)/16\) from the never-treated cells; its third diagonal is the sum of \(6/16\) and \(3(2+2xr)/16\).  These checks account for the shared-cell covariances.

Let \(B(x)=16\Gamma(x)/3\).  Its successive leading principal minors are
\[
 2,\qquad 3,\qquad \det B(x)=6-2x^2r^2=6-2r^2.
\tag{Q8}
\]
They are all positive because \(r^2<7/9<3\).  Gaussian elimination without row exchanges factors \(B(x)=L D L'\), where \(L\) is nonsingular and the diagonal pivots of \(D\) are the successive leading-minor ratios
\[
 2,\qquad \frac32,\qquad \frac{6-2r^2}{3}.
\]
All pivots are positive, so \(v'B(x)v=(L'v)'D(L'v)>0\) for every nonzero \(v\).  This proves the needed instance of Sylvester's criterion and shows that \(B(x)\), and hence \(\Gamma(x)\), is positive definite.  Since \(X\) has only two support points,
\[
 \min_{x\in\{-1,1\}}\lambda_{\min}\{\Gamma(x)\}>0
\tag{Q9}
\]
for each fixed admissible \(r\).  In addition, if \(d=(1,-1,0)'\), then \(d'\Gamma(x)d=3/8\).  Thus, up to the irrelevant sign of the one-column orthonormal basis \(N=d/\sqrt2\), \(H(x)=3/16\); the fixed-rank and positive-spectrum requirements used below hold.

The feasibility equations are \(b_1+b_2=\omega_1\) and \(b_3=\omega_2\), so every feasible loading is uniquely
\[
 b(q)=\bigl(\omega_1/2+q,\ \omega_1/2-q,\ \omega_2\bigr)'.
\tag{Q10}
\]
Using (Q7) and differentiating this scalar quadratic gives
\[
 \frac{d}{dq}\{b(q)'\Gamma(x)b(q)\}
 =2d'\Gamma(x)b(q)
 =\frac34\left\{q-\frac{(1+xr)\omega_2}{2}\right\},
 \qquad
 \frac{d^2}{dq^2}\{b(q)'\Gamma(x)b(q)\}=\frac34.
\tag{Q11}
\]
The strict positivity of the second derivative proves
\[
 q^\star(x)=\frac{(1+xr)\omega_2}{2},
 \qquad b^\star(x)=b\{q^\star(x)\}.
\tag{Q12}
\]
This also verifies the defining conditional quadratic program directly, without relying merely on the nonsingular formula in Lemma \(\ref{lem:singular-operator}\).

Averaging (Q7) over the symmetric binary \(X\) deletes precisely the terms containing \(xr\).  Equation (Q11) then makes the unique best joint constant loading \(b(\omega_2/2)\).  The published componentwise rule instead minimizes the first target block using a covariance proportional to
\(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{smallmatrix}\right)\).  Subject to \(b_1+b_2=\omega_1\), its unique minimum has \(b_1=b_2=\omega_1/2\); the singleton second block forces \(b_3=\omega_2\).  Hence
\[
 b^{\mathrm{const}}=b(\omega_2/2),
 \qquad b^{\mathrm{OVS}}=b(0).
\tag{Q13}
\]

The exact quadratic remainder from (Q11) is
\[
 E_P\!\left[b(q)'\Gamma(X)b(q)
 -b\{q^\star(X)\}'\Gamma(X)b\{q^\star(X)\}\right]
 =\frac38E_P\!\left[\left\{q-\frac{(1+Xr)\omega_2}{2}\right\}^2\right].
\tag{Q14}
\]
Since \(E_P[X]=0\) and \(E_P[X^2]=1\), this is
\[
 \frac38\left(q-\frac{\omega_2}{2}\right)^2
 +\frac{3r^2\omega_2^2}{32}.
\tag{Q15}
\]

We finally establish that (Q15) is a loss relative to the published bound, rather than only to a selected score family.  At period two the published clean set is \(\{3,\infty\}\), so it produces the single nonzero row \((2,3,\infty)\); at period three its clean set is the singleton \(\{\infty\}\).  The localized construction has the same single row: target \((2,2)\) permits both comparisons, whereas target \((2,3)\) permits only \(\infty\).  The deterministic row conventions and the identical standardized-residual formula therefore give
\[
 Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}=Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}=Z_{2;3,\infty,P}.
\tag{Q16}
\]
Furthermore, direct subtraction of the first two columns of (Q5), with the common target-share correction canceling, gives
\[
 R_{(2,2),3,P}-R_{(2,2),\infty,P}=-Z_{2;3,\infty,P}.
\tag{Q17}
\]
The kernel of \(A'\) is spanned by \(d\), so (Q17) proves that \(\mathcal C_P\) is exactly the closed measurable span of the normal in (Q16).  The conditions for Theorem \(\ref{thm:observable-equivalence}\) were verified above; its two tangent-exhaustion identities now yield
\[
 \mathcal C_P=\mathcal T_P^\perp=\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp.
\tag{Q18}
\]
Lemma \(\ref{lem:singular-operator}\) gives \(N'\Gamma(X)b^\star(X)=0\).  Since \(E_P[N'R_P\mid X]=0\), this says that \(\phi_{\mathrm{agg},P}=b^\star(X)'\Psi_P\) is orthogonal to \(\mathcal C_P\), while its difference from \(\psi_P^0\) belongs to \(\mathcal C_P\).  Thus it is the residual from projecting \(\psi_P^0\) on \(\mathcal C_P\).  Uniqueness of orthogonal projections and (Q18) now imply
\[
 \phi_{\mathrm{agg},P}=\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}=\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P},
 \qquad
 \Delta_{\mathrm{normal}}(P)=\Delta_{\mathrm{model}}(P)=0.
\tag{Q19}
\]
Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\) supplies the published-bound interpretation in (Q19), and Proposition \(\ref{prop:equality-frontier}\), together with (Q15), gives
\[
 \Delta\{b(q)\}
 =\frac38\left(q-\frac{\omega_2}{2}\right)^2
 +\frac{3r^2\omega_2^2}{32}.
\tag{Q20}
\]
Substitution of the two values in (Q13) yields
\[
 \Delta(b^{\mathrm{const}})=\frac{3r^2\omega_2^2}{32}>0,
 \qquad
 \Delta(b^{\mathrm{OVS}})=\frac{3(1+r^2)\omega_2^2}{32}>0,
\tag{Q21}
\]
where strictness uses \(r>0\) and \(\omega_2\ne0\).  At \(r=\omega_2=1/2\), these values are \(3/512\) and \(15/512\).  The first is the minimum over every deterministic feasible loading by the strict convexity in (Q11), completing the proof.

statements.statement: If every \(\mathcal J_k\) is a singleton, then \(M=K_0\), \(N\) has no columns, and the affine constraint has a unique loading.  If \(X\) is degenerate, then the conditional aggregate score-family minimizer equals the minimum-Euclidean-norm best constant joint loading \(b^{\mathrm{const}}\).  No identification with an externally published efficient influence function is asserted without a theorem-level source transcription and without tangent exhaustion.
statements.justification: The reduction theorem now consumes an exact, source-transcribed two-period panel-DDD equivalence and retains the singular constant-covariate loading check.
statements.gap: The exact external equality is limited to the just-identified two-period specialization; no unsupported staggered-DiD tangent-space equivalence is made.
statements.consumer: These reductions are mathematical and package-level regression tests for score signs, propensity ratios, target-share correction, and Moore--Penrose conventions.
statements.proof_tex:
Suppose first that every \(\mathcal J_k\) is a singleton.  By the definitions of \(M\) and \(K_0\),
\[
M=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}|\mathcal J_k|
=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}1
=|\mathcal K|=K_0.
\tag{K1}
\]
There is exactly one row of \(A\) for each \(k\), and that row has a one in the column indexed by \(k\) and zeros elsewhere.  Thus, after matching the fixed row order to the target order, \(A=I_{K_0}\); under another fixed order, \(A\) is a permutation matrix.  In either case \(A\) is square and nonsingular, so
\[
\ker(A')=\{0\},\qquad M-K_0=0.
\tag{K2}
\]
The definition of \(N\) therefore gives the zero-column matrix, and \(A'b=\omega\) has the unique solution \(b=(A')^{-1}\omega\).  Hence neither the conditional nor the constant program has a comparison-contrast direction.  Proposition \(\ref{prop:two-period-eif-reduction}\) supplies the source-transcribed two-period, one-target instance of this just-identified reduction, with canonicality only in the finite-support regime stated there.

Now suppose that \(X\) is degenerate.  Conditioning on \(X\) is then conditioning on the trivial sigma-field.  Because the corrected score vector belongs to \(L_2^0(P)^M\), the definitions of \(\Gamma\) and \(\Omega\) give
\[
\Gamma(X)
=\operatorname{Cov}_P(\Psi_P\mid X)
=\operatorname{Cov}_P(\Psi_P)
=E_P[\Psi_P\Psi_P']
=\Omega
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\tag{K3}
\]
Thus the conditional and constant programs minimize the same positive-semidefinite quadratic form over the same affine set.  It remains to show that their singular-case selectors coincide.

Since \(A\) has full column rank, \(b^0=A(A'A)^{-1}\omega\) is feasible.  Every feasible vector has a unique representation
\[
b=b^0+Nz,
\qquad z\in\mathbb R^{M-K_0},
\tag{K4}
\]
because feasibility is equivalent to \(b-b^0\in\ker(A')\), and the columns of \(N\) are an orthonormal basis of that kernel.  Set
\[
H=N'\Gamma N,
\qquad d=N'\Gamma b^0.
\]
Expanding the common objective in (K4) yields
\[
(b^0+Nz)'\Gamma(b^0+Nz)
=(b^0)'\Gamma b^0+2z'd+z'Hz.
\tag{K5}
\]
The matrix \(H\) is symmetric positive semidefinite.  If \(v\in\ker H\), then
\[
0=v'Hv=(Nv)'\Gamma(Nv).
\]
For any \(w\in\mathbb R^M\) and any scalar \(t\), positive semidefiniteness gives
\[
0\le (Nv+tw)'\Gamma(Nv+tw)
=2t w'\Gamma Nv+t^2w'\Gamma w.
\]
If \(w'\Gamma Nv\ne0\), choosing \(t\) with the opposite sign and sufficiently small magnitude would make the right-hand side negative.  Therefore \(w'\Gamma Nv=0\) for every \(w\), so \(\Gamma Nv=0\).  Consequently
\[
v'd=(Nv)'\Gamma b^0=0.
\]
Thus \(d\perp\ker H\).  Since \(H\) is symmetric, \((\ker H)^\perp=\operatorname{range}H\), proving
\[
d\in\operatorname{range}H.
\tag{K6}
\]
The first-order equation for the convex quadratic (K5) is \(Hz=-d\).  By (K6), all and only its solutions are
\[
z=-H^\dagger d+v,
\qquad v\in\ker H.
\tag{K7}
\]
Necessity follows by differentiating (K5).  Conversely, if \(Hz=-d\), then replacing \(z\) by \(z+u\) changes (K5) by \(u'Hu\ge0\), proving sufficiency.

For the conditional selector, the requirement in Definition \(\ref{def:canonical-loading}\) is
\[
N'(b-b^0)=z\in\operatorname{range}H.
\tag{K8}
\]
In (K7), \(-H^\dagger d\in\operatorname{range}H\), while \(v\in\ker H\), and the two subspaces are orthogonal.  Hence (K8) holds if and only if \(v=0\).  Therefore
\[
b^\star=b^0-NH^\dagger N'\Gamma b^0.
\tag{K9}
\]
For the constant selector, \(b^0\in\operatorname{col}A\), whereas \(NH^\dagger d\) and \(Nv\) lie in \(\ker(A')=(\operatorname{col}A)^\perp\).  Orthonormality of the columns of \(N\), together with \(H^\dagger d\perp v\), gives
\[
\|b^0-NH^\dagger d+Nv\|_2^2
=\|b^0\|_2^2+\|H^\dagger d\|_2^2+\|v\|_2^2.
\tag{K10}
\]
The unique minimum-Euclidean-norm minimizer is therefore obtained at \(v=0\).  By the equivalent argmin characterization in the definition of \(b^{\mathrm{const}}\), (K9) is also \(b^{\mathrm{const}}\).  Together with (K3), this proves
\[
b^\star=b^{\mathrm{const}}
\quad\text{when \(X\) is degenerate},
\]
including singular cases.  Formula (K9) agrees with the singular operator representation in Lemma \(\ref{lem:singular-operator}\) whenever its fixed-rank regularity conditions are invoked.

Finally, Proposition \(\ref{prop:two-period-eif-reduction}\) establishes the only equality claimed here with externally published efficient influence functions from the theorem-level transcriptions of the two panel-DDD results.  At the fixed-finite-support laws specified in that proposition, canonicality in the present observed-law model follows from the tangent exhaustion in Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\), rather than from algebraic resemblance.  The proposition makes no tangent-space nesting claim for the separate staggered-DiD result.  This proves the theorem's final qualification.

statements.statement: Does there exist a confidence procedure based on the rank-adaptive spectral handle for \(K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)\) over an explicitly specified class of local law sequences \((P_n)\) such that: (i) its coverage for \(\tau_\omega(P_n)\) is uniformly asymptotically at least \(1-\alpha\); (ii) a declared expected-length, diameter, or local-power criterion rules out the vacuous interval \(\mathbb R\); (iii) the class gives quantitative envelopes for the smallest positive eigenvalue of \(K_{\mathrm{OVS},P_n}(X)\), for covariate sets of positive \(P_{n,X}\)-probability on which rank changes, and for nuisance and conditional-moment errors relative to \(\lambda_n\); and (iv) at every fixed finite-support law whose positive spectrum is separated, the procedure is asymptotically equivalent to \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}\) and its existing Wald interval?  This question concerns the published canonical-projection operator only; rank changes in the comparator KKT systems are a separate efficiency-gap inference problem.
statements.justification: Rank changes in the published conditional normal operator are the nonregular boundary relevant to the attaining estimator; they cannot be hidden inside a fixed-rank pointwise theorem, and coverage must be paired with a length or power criterion to be nonvacuous.
statements.gap: The established finite-support result treats only fixed laws with separated positive rank.  Neither the staggered DiD and DDD literature nor this note supplies uniform inference over declared local sequences with weak or changing eigenvalues of the published normal operator under explicit nuisance envelopes and a nonvacuity criterion.
statements.consumer: A solution would stabilize the optional efficient target-inference backend when published OVS normal directions are nearly redundant.  Comparator-KKT rank adaptation would remain a separate extension for efficiency-gap inference.

obligation.what_is_open: A nonvacuous uniformly valid confidence procedure has not been characterized over an explicitly specified local-sequence class in which positive eigenvalues of \(K_{\mathrm{OVS},P_n}(X)\) may approach zero or its rank may change on covariate sets of positive probability.
obligation.obstruction: The map \((K,r)\mapsto K^\dagger r\) has no uniform perturbation modulus near a rank change without quantitative compatibility: in a vanishing-eigenvalue direction \(v\), the coefficient is \(v'r/\lambda\), whereas the exact-law range condition at \(\lambda=0\) alone supplies no local bound on this ratio.  The fixed-support estimates have only pointwise error control, and coverage alone admits the vacuous interval \(\mathbb R\).  Thus a local eigenvalue/nuisance envelope and an expected-length, diameter, or power criterion are mathematically necessary to pose either a positive construction or an impossibility theorem.
obligation.attempted: The fixed-rank argument was transferred from the obsolete aggregate operator to the actual published system.  Proposition \(\mathrm{\ref{prop:ovs-normal-finite-support-rates}}\) controls \(\widehat K_{\mathrm{OVS}}-K_{\mathrm{OVS}}\) and \(\widehat r_{\mathrm{OVS}}-r_{\mathrm{OVS}}\) at root-\(n\) rate and recovers rank at each separated fixed law.  Extending the Moore--Penrose perturbation calculation to local eigenvalues introduces reciprocal powers of the smallest retained eigenvalue, so the available remainder is not uniform without declared eigenvalue and nuisance envelopes.  No comparator-KKT calculation is relevant to target-estimator adaptation.
obligation.partial_result: Fix a conditional-mean interior law induced by the global OVS model.  Suppose that \(X\) has fixed finite support with every support mass bounded below, all first stages are training-cell averages, sampling is independent and identically distributed with fixed \(T\), retained-cell overlap and the unconditional and global conditional fourth-moment envelopes hold, cross-fitting uses a fixed number of folds, and \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}>0\).  Because the support of \(X\) is finite, at this fixed law the positive eigenvalues of \(K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x)\), when present, have a positive minimum over support points.  Proposition~\ref{prop:ovs-normal-finite-support-rates} then gives consistent rank recovery and root-\(n\) estimation of \(K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\) and \(r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\) on the recovered-rank event.  With the existing deterministic threshold \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\), \(0<a<1/4\), Theorem~\ref{thm:crossfit-attainment} gives the pointwise expansion and Wald limit for \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}\).  The proposed rank-adaptive procedure is required to agree asymptotically with that estimator and interval at every such fixed law; no uniform statement is obtained as the positive spectrum approaches zero or the rank changes.

statements.statement: If \(Z_1,Z_2,\ldots\) are independent and identically distributed real random variables with \(E[Z_1]=0\) and \(0<E[Z_1^2]<\infty\), then \(n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n Z_i\Rightarrow N(0,E[Z_1^2])\).

source.verbatim_statement: Let Y₁, …, Yₙ be i.i.d. random variables with E Y₁ = 0 and E Y₁² = 1. Then √n Ȳₙ converges in distribution to the standard normal distribution.

statements.statement:
Let \(P\) satisfy retained-cell overlap and the fourth-moment condition, and let \(P_\epsilon\) be any regular dominated observed-law submodel through \(P=P_0\) with score \(s\in L_2^0(P)\).  For
\[
\psi_P^0(O)=\sum_{k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K}\omega_k\Psi_{k,c_0(k),P}(O),
\]
the observable functional \(\tau_\omega(P)=\omega'\theta(P)\) is pathwise differentiable along the submodel and
\[
\left.\frac{d}{d\epsilon}\tau_\omega(P_\epsilon)\right|_{\epsilon=0}
=E_P[\psi_P^0(O)s(O)].
\]
In particular, \(\psi_P^0\) is a mean-zero ambient observed-law gradient of the identified aggregate.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(k=(g,t)\), write \(c=c_0(k)\), and put \(\mu_k=E_P[p_{g,1}(X)q_{k,c}(X)]\), so \(\theta_k=\mu_k/\pi_{g,1}\).  Overlap bounds every inverse propensity, while the fourth-moment assumption and Jensen's inequality give the integrability needed to differentiate the finite sums and expectations along a regular dominated submodel.

Writing a dot for a derivative at zero, quotient differentiation gives
\[
\dot p_{a,v}(x)=E_P[(\mathbf 1_{a,v}-p_{a,v}(x))s(O)\mid X=x]
\tag{R1}
\]
and
\[
\dot m_{a,v,u}(x)
=\frac{E_P[\mathbf 1_{a,v}\{\Delta Y_u-m_{a,v,u}(x)\}s(O)\mid X=x]}{p_{a,v}(x)}.
\tag{R2}
\]
Differentiating \(\mu_k\) gives
\[
\dot\mu_k=E_P[p_{g,1}q_{k,c}s]+E_P[\dot p_{g,1}q_{k,c}]+E_P[p_{g,1}\dot q_{k,c}].
\tag{R3}
\]
The first two terms combine, by (R1) and iterated expectation, to \(E_P[\mathbf 1_{g,1}q_{k,c}s]\).  For example, the \(m_{g,0,u}\) contribution from (R2) is
\[
-E_P\!\left[\frac{p_{g,1}(X)}{p_{g,0}(X)}\mathbf 1_{g,0}
\{\Delta Y_u-m_{g,0,u}(X)\}s(O)\right],
\]
and the other three cell contributions have the signs in Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\).  Summing over \(u\) gives
\[
\dot\mu_k=E_P[\pi_{g,1}R_{k,c,P}(O)s(O)].
\tag{R4}
\]
Also \(\dot\pi_{g,1}=E_P[\mathbf 1_{g,1}s]\), since \(E_P[s]=0\).  Because \(\pi_{g,1}>0\), another quotient rule gives
\[
\dot\theta_k
=\frac{\dot\mu_k-\theta_k\dot\pi_{g,1}}{\pi_{g,1}}
=E_P\!\left[\left\{R_{k,c,P}-\frac{\theta_k}{\pi_{g,1}}\mathbf 1_{g,1}\right\}s\right]
=E_P[\Psi_{k,c,P}s].
\tag{R5}
\]
The bracket has mean zero because \(E_P[R_{k,c,P}]=\theta_k\).  Multiplying by fixed \(\omega_k\) and summing over finite \(\mathcal K\) proves the claim.
statements.justification: This calculation establishes that the denominator-corrected reference score represents the derivative before any tangent-space projection is invoked.
statements.gap: The pairwise score formula alone does not prove that it differentiates the ratio target when target-cell shares vary.
statements.consumer: The complete-normal theorem uses this ambient gradient as the object projected onto the observed tangent space.

statements.statement:
Let \(P\) be a conditional-mean interior observed law induced by a full-data law in the global OVS model \(\mathcal M\).  Suppose \(X\) has fixed finite support with positive mass at every support point.  Under global retained-cell overlap, the fourth-moment condition, fixed contrast rank, and the contrast spectral gap,
\[
\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp
=\overline{\{a(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O):a\text{ measurable and }
E_P[(a(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O))^2]<\infty\}}^{L_2(P)}.
\]
With the objects in Definition \(\ref{def:ovs-normal-projection}\),
\[
\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}
=\psi_P^0-r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)'K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)^\dagger
Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}
\tag{15}
\]
is the canonical gradient of \(\tau_\omega\) in the published class at \(P\), including singular and redundant fixed-law cases, and
\[
V_{\mathrm{OVS}}
=E_P[(\psi_P^0)^2]
-E_P[r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)'K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)^\dagger r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)].
\tag{16}
\]
The former complete-normal gradient \(\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}\) is the canonical gradient in the larger localized observed model \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{loc}}\) at this finite-support law.  It remains a valid gradient in the published subclass, but
\[
V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\le V_{\mathrm{can}},
\qquad
V_{\mathrm{can}}-V_{\mathrm{OVS}}
=E_P[(\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}-\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P})^2],
\tag{17}
\]
with equality if and only if
\[
E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}\mid X]=0
\quad P_X\text{-almost surely}.
\tag{18}
\]

The conditional loading \(b^\star\) remains the singular-safe optimum inside the aggregate pairwise-score family.  In particular,
\[
V_{\mathrm{agg}}
=\operatorname{Var}_P\{\omega'h(X)\}
+E_P[b^\star(X)'\Gamma_P(X)b^\star(X)],
\tag{19}
\]
and every measurable feasible \(b\), with \(A'b(X)=\omega\) almost surely and \(b(X)'\Psi_P\in L_2(P)\), satisfies
\[
\operatorname{Var}_P\{b(X)'\Psi_P\}-V_{\mathrm{agg}}
=E_P[(b(X)-b^\star(X))'\Gamma_P(X)(b(X)-b^\star(X))]\ge0.
\tag{20}
\]
The three nested frontiers obey
\[
V_{\mathrm{agg}}-V_{\mathrm{OVS}}
=E_P[(\phi_{\mathrm{agg},P}-\phi_{\mathrm{can},P})^2]
+E_P[(\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}-\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P})^2].
\tag{21}
\]
Thus \(b^\star(X)'\Psi_P\) reaches the localized bound exactly when \(E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\phi_{\mathrm{agg},P}\mid X]=0\), and it reaches the published OVS bound exactly when
\[
E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\phi_{\mathrm{agg},P}\mid X]=0
\quad P_X\text{-almost surely}.
\tag{22}
\]
Accordingly, score-family projection is not called semiparametric efficiency unless (22) is verified.  No canonical-gradient claim is made here for continuously distributed \(X\).
statements.justification: At fixed finite-support covariate laws, the theorem combines tangent exhaustion with the singular Moore--Penrose projection to derive \(\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\) and the ordered published, localized, and aggregate frontiers.
statements.gap: Canonicality is not established for continuously distributed covariates; moreover \(b^\star(X)'\Psi_P\) is only aggregate-family optimal unless its published-normal equation holds.
statements.consumer: The fixed-support attaining estimator, equality diagnostics, corrected witness, finite-support gap functional, and two-period reduction use the published canonical gradient.
statements.proof_tex:
The first tangent-normal identity is equation (2) of Theorem \(\ref{thm:observable-equivalence}\), whose hypotheses include the finite-support, overlap, fourth-moment, and conditional-mean-interior conditions imposed here.  Lemma \(\ref{lem:reference-score-gradient}\) gives, for every \(s\in\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}\),
\[
\dot\tau_{\omega,P}[s]=E_P[\psi_P^0s].
\tag{T1}
\]
Abbreviate \(Z=Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\), \(K=K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\), and \(r=r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\).  If \(v\in\ker K(x)\), then
\[
0=v'K(x)v=E_P[(v'Z)^2\mid X=x].
\]
Thus \(v'Z=0\) conditionally almost surely and \(v'r(x)=E_P[v'Z\psi_P^0\mid X=x]=0\).  Since \(K(x)\) is symmetric,
\[
r(x)\in\operatorname{range}K(x),
\qquad K(x)K(x)^\dagger r(x)=r(x).
\tag{T2}
\]
The Moore--Penrose map is measurable at this fixed finite-support law; explicitly, for every symmetric matrix,
\[
K^\dagger=\lim_{j\to\infty}(K^2+j^{-1}I)^{-1}K.
\tag{T3}
\]
Put \(p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}=r'K^\dagger Z\).  Symmetry, (T2), and the Moore--Penrose identities imply
\[
E_P[p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}^2\mid X]
=r'K^\dagger KK^\dagger r
=r'K^\dagger r
=E_P[\psi_P^0p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\mid X].
\tag{T4}
\]
Conditional Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
E_P[p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}^2\mid X]
\le E_P[(\psi_P^0)^2\mid X],
\]
where the assertion is immediate when the left side is zero and otherwise follows after division by its square root.  Since Lemma \(\ref{lem:reference-score-gradient}\) and the moment assumptions give \(\psi_P^0\in L_2(P)\), this proves \(p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\in L_2(P)\).  For every square-integrable measurable multiple \(a(X)'Z\),
\[
E_P[(\psi_P^0-p_{\mathrm{OVS},P})a(X)'Z]
=E_P[a(X)'\{r-KK^\dagger r\}]=0.
\tag{T5}
\]
Equations (T4)--(T5), first on the generating set and then on its \(L_2(P)\)-closure, and tangent exhaustion give
\[
p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}=\Pi_{\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp}\psi_P^0,
\qquad
\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}=\Pi_{\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}}\psi_P^0.
\tag{T6}
\]
Combining (T1) and (T6) proves canonicality.  Taking expectations in (T4) and expanding \(E_P[(\psi_P^0-p_{\mathrm{OVS},P})^2]\) proves (16).  Coefficients that differ by an element of \(\ker K(X)\) have the same product with \(Z\), so singular or redundant coordinates create no ambiguity in the projected random variable.

The same calculation with \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\), using equation (3) of Theorem \(\ref{thm:observable-equivalence}\), gives
\[
p_{\mathrm{per},P}=\Pi_{\mathcal T_P^\perp}\psi_P^0,
\qquad
\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}=\Pi_{\mathcal T_P}\psi_P^0.
\tag{T7}
\]
Theorem \(\ref{thm:observable-equivalence}\) gives \(\mathcal T_P^\perp\subseteq\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp\).  For nested closed subspaces, the difference between the two orthogonal projections lies in the larger normal space and is orthogonal to the smaller projection residual.  Applying this elementary fact here yields
\[
\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}
=\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}+(p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}-p_{\mathrm{per},P}),
\qquad
E_P[\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}-p_{\mathrm{per},P})]=0.
\]
Pythagoras proves (17).  Moreover, \(p_{\mathrm{per},P}\in\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp\), so subtracting it from the ambient gradient leaves a valid gradient on the published tangent space.  It is the published canonical gradient exactly when it is orthogonal to the published normal closure.  Because \(Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\) has finitely many coordinates, iterated expectation makes this equivalent to (18).

On the observable equality model, every residual in Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) has conditional mean zero, and every clean comparison in a target block has the same conditional contrast.  Therefore
\[
E_P[\Psi_P\mid X]=Ah(X).
\tag{T8}
\]
Every feasible loading has conditional mean \(\omega'h(X)\), by \(A'b(X)=\omega\).  The conditional variance identity and Definition \(\ref{def:canonical-loading}\) yield
\[
\operatorname{Var}_P\{b(X)'\Psi_P\}
=\operatorname{Var}_P\{\omega'h(X)\}
+E_P[b(X)'\Gamma_P(X)b(X)].
\tag{T9}
\]
Lemma \(\ref{lem:singular-operator}\), using Assumptions \(\ref{ass:fixed-contrast-rank}\) and \(\ref{ass:contrast-spectral-gap}\), gives \(A'b^\star=\omega\) and \(N'\Gamma b^\star=0\).  If \(d=b-b^\star\), then \(A'd=0\).  Since the columns of \(N\) form a basis of \(\ker A'\), there is a measurable \(z(X)\) with \(d=Nz\), and hence \(d'\Gamma b^\star=z'N'\Gamma b^\star=0\).  Expanding the quadratic term in (T9) proves (19)--(20), including the singular fixed-rank case.

Let \(b^{\mathrm{ref}}\) put weight \(\omega_k\) on coordinate \((k,c_0(k))\) and zero on every other coordinate.  Then \(\psi_P^0=b^{\mathrm{ref}\prime}\Psi_P\).  Feasibility gives \(b^{\mathrm{ref}}-b^\star\in\operatorname{col}N\), and the target-share correction in \(\Psi\) is constant within each target block and is annihilated by \(N'\).  Therefore
\[
p_{\mathrm{agg},P}:=\psi_P^0-\phi_{\mathrm{agg},P}
=(b^{\mathrm{ref}}-b^\star(X))'R_P\in\mathcal C_P.
\tag{T10}
\]
Using \(N'R=N'\Psi\), (T8), \(N'A=0\), and \(N'\Gamma b^\star=0\), we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_P[N'R_P\phi_{\mathrm{agg},P}\mid X]
&=N'E_P[\Psi_P\Psi_P'\mid X]b^\star\\
&=N'\{\Gamma_P+Ahh'A'\}b^\star=0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{T11}
\]
Thus \(p_{\mathrm{agg},P}=\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\psi_P^0\).  The nested closed normal spaces from Theorem \(\ref{thm:observable-equivalence}\),
\[
\mathcal C_P\subseteq\mathcal T_P^\perp
\subseteq\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp,
\]
have orthogonal successive projection increments.  Expanding the squared norms of their projection residuals proves (21).  Finally, a square-integrable variable is orthogonal to every square-integrable measurable multiple of a finite normal vector \(Z\) if and only if its conditional cross-moment with \(Z\) is zero: the forward implication follows by testing with bounded support-cell multiples, and the reverse implication follows by iterated expectation and closure.  Applying this equivalence to \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\) and \(Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\) proves the two equality characterizations, including (22).  Hence \(\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\), rather than \(b^\star(X)'\Psi_P\) absent (22), is the canonical gradient proved by the finite-support tangent exhaustion.

Write the fixed support as \(\{x_1,\ldots,x_D\}\), and put \(\nu_d=P(X=x_d)\).  The asserted lower support-mass bound and retained-cell overlap imply
\[
P(X=x_d,G=a,S=s)=\nu_d p_{a,s}(x_d)\ge \underline\nu\varepsilon>0
\tag{37a}
\]
for every retained \((d,a,s)\).  Under the stated fixed-fold construction, every training complement contains order \(n\) observations.  For any one of the finitely many cell variables \(W\) used below, let \(\widehat E_{-\ell}[W\mid a,s,x_d]\) denote its training-cell mean.  Conditional fourth moments of \(\Delta Y_u\), retained-cell overlap, and fixed \(T\) imply finite second moments for: indicators; indicator-weighted increments; products of two increments; and every fixed finite linear combination of these variables.  Chebyshev's inequality applied to their empirical numerators and denominators, followed by the elementary ratio identity
\[
\frac{A_n}{B_n}-\frac{A}{B}
=\frac{A_n-A}{B_n}+\frac{A(B-B_n)}{BB_n},
\tag{37b}
\]
on the event \(B_n\ge B/2\), proves, uniformly over the finite sets of folds, support points, cells, periods, and coordinates,
\[
\widehat p_{a,s}^{-\ell}(x_d)-p_{a,s}(x_d)=O_P(n^{-1/2}),
\qquad
\widehat m_{a,s,u}^{-\ell}(x_d)-m_{a,s,u}(x_d)=O_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{37c}
\]
The same argument gives the root-\(n\) rate for every training preliminary target ratio and every empirical conditional raw moment of degree at most two in the increments.  Since \(D\) and all vector dimensions are fixed,
\[
\|f\|_{P_X,4}\le \max_{1\le d\le D}|f(x_d)|
\tag{37d}
\]
coordinatewise, so the same rates hold in all displayed \(L_4(P_X)\) norms.

We next pass from the primitive cell moments to the two learned conditional moments.  On the event supplied by (37a)--(37c), all clipped reciprocals are bounded by \(2/\varepsilon\).  The explicit formulas in Definitions \(\ref{def:orthogonal-ovs-normal-signal}\) and \(\ref{def:crossfit-estimator}\) are then finite sums and products of the empirical quantities in (37c), bounded reciprocals, and conditional raw moments of degree at most two.  Repeated use of
\[
ab-a_0b_0=(a-a_0)b_0+a_0(b-b_0)+(a-a_0)(b-b_0)
\tag{37e}
\]
shows entry by entry that
\[
\widehat K_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}(x_d)-K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x_d)
=O_P(n^{-1/2}),
\qquad
\widehat r_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}(x_d)-r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x_d)
=O_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{37f}
\]
This calculation includes the off-diagonal products of score coordinates sharing an outcome cell; they are empirical cross-products in (37e), not omitted blockwise terms.  Taking the finite maximum, using equivalence of finite-dimensional matrix norms, and applying (37d) proves (37).

It remains to justify thresholding and the coefficient rate, including singular cases.  Fix a support point and abbreviate
\[
K=K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x_d),\quad
\widehat K=\widehat K_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}(x_d),\quad
r=r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x_d),\quad
\widehat r=\widehat r_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}(x_d).
\]
Both \(K\) and \(\widehat K\) are symmetric positive semidefinite second-moment matrices.  For ordered eigenvalues, the variational characterization of eigenvalues and the inequality \(|v'(\widehat K-K)v|\le\|\widehat K-K\|_{\mathrm{op}}\) for \(\|v\|=1\) give
\[
|\lambda_j(\widehat K)-\lambda_j(K)|
\le\|\widehat K-K\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{38a}
\]
At the fixed law, the minimum over all positive eigenvalues of all \(K(x_d)\) is a strictly positive number \(\delta_P\), with the zero-rank convention if no such eigenvalue exists.  Since \(n^{-1/2}/\tau_n\to0\) and \(\tau_n\to0\), (38a) implies simultaneously over the finite support and folds that every population zero eigenvalue is below \(\tau_n\) and every positive eigenvalue is above \(\tau_n\), with probability tending to one.  This proves rank recovery.

The population right-hand side is compatible with the singular system.  Indeed, if \(v\in\ker K\), then
\[
0=v'Kv=E_P[(v'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}})^2\mid X=x_d],
\]
so \(v'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}=0\) conditionally almost surely and consequently \(v'r=E_P[v'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\psi_P^0\mid X=x_d]=0\).  Thus \(r\in\operatorname{range}K\), and \(\alpha=K^\dagger r\) is the unique solution in \(\operatorname{range}K\).

At a support point where \(K\) has rank zero, rank recovery makes the retained matrix zero, so \(\widehat\alpha=\alpha=0\) and the coefficient-rate conclusion is immediate.  Consider a positive-rank support point.  On the rank-recovery event let \(\Pi\) and \(\widehat\Pi\) be the orthogonal projectors onto the ranges of \(K\) and the retained \(\widehat K\).  When \(\|\widehat K-K\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\delta_P/4\), every retained eigenvalue is at least \(\delta_P/2\).  If \(\widehat u\) is a retained unit eigenvector and \(Q=I-\Pi\), then
\[
\lambda(\widehat K)Q\widehat u
=Q\widehat K\widehat u
=Q(\widehat K-K)\widehat u,
\]
because \(QK=0\).  Hence \(\|Q\widehat u\|\le 2\|\widehat K-K\|_{\mathrm{op}}/\delta_P\).  Applying this to a retained orthonormal basis, and using equality of the two nonzero principal-angle spectra for equal-rank subspaces, gives
\[
\|\widehat\Pi-\Pi\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le C_P\|\widehat K-K\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\tag{38b}
\]
This is an elementary consequence of the displayed eigenvector equation, rather than an extra rank or spectral assumption.

Since \(\|\widehat K_\tau^\dagger\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2/\delta_P\) on this event and \(\widehat K_\tau^\dagger\widehat K=\widehat\Pi\), the identities \(r=K\alpha\) and \(\Pi\alpha=\alpha\) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat\alpha-\alpha
&=\widehat K_\tau^\dagger(\widehat r-r)
+\widehat K_\tau^\dagger(K-\widehat K)\alpha
+(\widehat\Pi-\Pi)\alpha.
\end{aligned}
\tag{38c}
\]
Equations (37f), (38b), and (38c) yield \(\widehat\alpha-\alpha=O_P(n^{-1/2})\) at each support point.  The finite maximum and (37d) give the stated sharper \(L_4(P_X)\) rate uniformly over folds.  Since \(\tau_n\le1\) eventually, this sharper fixed-law statement also implies the conservative bound
\[
\|\widehat\alpha_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}
-K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}^\dagger r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\|_{P_X,4}
=O_P(n^{-1/2}/\tau_n),
\]
which is (38).  If \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\), the right side is \(O_P(n^{-1/2+a})\); its square is \(O_P(n^{-1+2a})=o_P(n^{-1/2})\) for \(a<1/4\), and its product with either rate in (37c) is \(O_P(n^{-1+a})=o_P(n^{-1/2})\) for the same range.  This proves all assertions.

Let \(z_0\in\mathbb R^d\), and let \(B_1(z),\ldots,B_L(z)\) be finitely many continuously differentiable real symmetric matrix maps near \(z_0\).  Suppose every nonzero eigenvalue of every \(B_j(z_0)\) has absolute value at least \(\kappa_0>0\).  If \(\widehat z-z_0=O_P(n^{-1/2})\), \(\tau_n\downarrow0\), and \(n^{-1/2}/\tau_n\to0\), then retaining exactly the empirical eigenvalues satisfying \(|\lambda|>\tau_n\) recovers all population ranks simultaneously with probability tending to one.  On that event each thresholded inverse equals a continuously differentiable selected-rank inverse branch.  Consequently any scalar \(F\) formed by finitely many additions, multiplications, divisions by quantities nonzero at \(z_0\), and these selected-rank inverses satisfies, with \(d_0=DF(z_0)\),
\[
F_{\tau_n}(\widehat z)-F(z_0)=d_0'(\widehat z-z_0)+o_P(n^{-1/2}).
\]
For a symmetric matrix coordinate \(B\), the selected-rank inverse derivative in direction \(H\) is
\[
DB_0^\sharp[H]
=-B_0^\dagger HB_0^\dagger
+(B_0^\dagger)^2H(I-B_0B_0^\dagger)
+(I-B_0^\dagger B_0)H(B_0^\dagger)^2.
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Because the collection of matrix maps is finite, it suffices first to treat one map and then intersect the resulting probability-one-asymptotic events.  Write \(B_0=B(z_0)\).  Continuous differentiability on a neighborhood of \(z_0\) gives a finite local Lipschitz constant, and \(\widehat z-z_0=O_P(n^{-1/2})\) therefore implies
\[
 \|B(\widehat z)-B_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_P(n^{-1/2})=o_P(\tau_n).
\tag{S1}
\]
For completeness, the eigenvalue perturbation bound needed here follows directly from the variational characterization.  For every unit vector \(v\),
\[
 |v'\{B(\widehat z)-B_0\}v|
 \le \|B(\widehat z)-B_0\|_{\mathrm{op}},
\]
and applying this inequality inside the successive minimum--maximum formulas for the ordered eigenvalues gives
\[
 \max_k|\lambda_k\{B(\widehat z)\}-\lambda_k(B_0)|
 \le \|B(\widehat z)-B_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\tag{S2}
\]
With probability tending to one, the right side of (S2) is smaller than \(\tau_n\), while \(\tau_n<\kappa_0/2\).  On that event, every eigenvalue descending from the zero cluster has absolute value below \(\tau_n\), and every eigenvalue descending from a nonzero population eigenvalue has absolute value at least \(\kappa_0/2>\tau_n\).  Thus absolute-value thresholding recovers the population rank.  Finiteness of the collection proves simultaneous recovery.

We next construct the local differentiable inverse branch rather than assuming it.  Choose a positively oriented circle \(\gamma\) centered at zero whose interior contains no nonzero eigenvalue of \(B_0\).  Shrinking the neighborhood if necessary, the resolvent exists on \(\gamma\) and the same circle separates the eigenvalue cluster emanating from zero from all remaining eigenvalues.  Define
\[
 P_0(z)=\frac{1}{2\pi\mathrm i}\int_\gamma(wI-B(z))^{-1}\,dw.
\tag{S3}
\]
The resolvent identity
\[
 (wI-B_1)^{-1}-(wI-B_2)^{-1}
 =(wI-B_1)^{-1}(B_1-B_2)(wI-B_2)^{-1}
\tag{S4}
\]
and differentiation of the inverse show directly that \(P_0(z)\) is continuously differentiable.  Diagonalizing the real symmetric matrix \(B(z)\) inside the integrand shows coordinatewise that the integral is one on the separated small-eigenvalue cluster and zero on its complement.  Hence \(P_0(z)\) is the orthogonal spectral projector onto that cluster.  Set
\[
 B^\sharp(z)
 =(I-P_0(z))\{B(z)+P_0(z)\}^{-1}(I-P_0(z)).
\tag{S5}
\]
The middle matrix is nonsingular near \(z_0\): it acts as \(B(z)\) on the separated nonzero cluster and as \(B(z)+I\) on the small cluster.  Equations (S3)--(S5) therefore make \(B^\sharp\) continuously differentiable.  At \(z_0\) it equals \(B_0^\dagger\), and on the rank-recovery event it agrees with the thresholded inverse by zeroing the small cluster and inverting every retained eigenvalue.

To compute its derivative, decompose the Euclidean space orthogonally as \(\operatorname{range}(B_0)\oplus\ker(B_0)\).  In this basis write
\[
 B_0=\begin{pmatrix}D&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 B_0^\dagger=\begin{pmatrix}D^{-1}&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 H=\begin{pmatrix}H_{11}&H_{12}\\H_{21}&H_{22}\end{pmatrix},
\]
where \(D\) is nonsingular.  Differentiating (S3)--(S5), block by block, gives
\[
 DB_0^\sharp[H]
 =\begin{pmatrix}
 -D^{-1}H_{11}D^{-1}&D^{-2}H_{12}\\
 H_{21}D^{-2}&0
 \end{pmatrix}.
\tag{S6}
\]
Multiplying the displayed block matrices verifies that (S6) is exactly
\[
 DB_0^\sharp[H]
 =-B_0^\dagger HB_0^\dagger
 +(B_0^\dagger)^2H(I-B_0B_0^\dagger)
 +(I-B_0^\dagger B_0)H(B_0^\dagger)^2.
\tag{S7}
\]

Every ordinary division appearing in \(F\) is continuously differentiable on a sufficiently small neighborhood because its denominator is nonzero at \(z_0\).  Equations (S5)--(S7), ordinary matrix calculus, and the chain rule thus show that the selected-rank composition \(F^\sharp\) is continuously differentiable at \(z_0\).  Its first-order expansion is
\[
 F^\sharp(\widehat z)-F^\sharp(z_0)
 =DF(z_0)'(\widehat z-z_0)+o_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{S8}
\]
On the simultaneous rank-recovery event, \(F_{\tau_n}(\widehat z)=F^\sharp(\widehat z)\), while \(F^\sharp(z_0)=F(z_0)\).  Substitution into (S8) proves the claimed expansion and completes the proof.
statements.justification: The finite-support gap functional contains positive-semidefinite normal matrices and indefinite comparator KKT matrices, so its operational derivative must threshold by absolute eigenvalue.
statements.gap: An ordinary inverse delta method does not cover redundant score coordinates.
statements.consumer: The fixed-support gap theorem uses the selected-rank derivative and simultaneous rank recovery.

statements.statement:
Fix a conditional-mean interior law \(P\) in the published OVS model.  Suppose \(X\) has fixed finite support with every support mass bounded below, retained-cell overlap and the fourth-moment condition hold, and \((O_i)_{i=1}^n\) are independent and identically distributed.  For a declared rule \(z\in\{\mathrm{OVS},\mathrm{const}\}\), let \(b_z(P)\) be the law-dependent comparator, define \(\mu(P)\), \(F_z\), and \(\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}\) by Definition \(\ref{def:gap-one-step}\), and take \(\tau_n\downarrow0\) with \(n^{-1/2}/\tau_n\to0\).  Let
\[
d_z=DF_z^\sharp\{\mu(P)\},
\qquad
\xi_z(O)=d_z'[U(O)-\mu(P)],
\qquad
V_{\Delta,z}=E_P[\xi_z(O)^2].
\]
If \(V_{\Delta,z}>0\), then
\[
F_z\{\mu(P)\}=\operatorname{Var}_P\{b_z(P)'\Psi_P(O)\}-V_{\mathrm{OVS}}
=\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},z}(P),
\tag{W1}
\]
\[
\sqrt n\{\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}-\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},z}(P)\}
=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_z(O_i)+o_P(1)
\ \Rightarrow\ N(0,V_{\Delta,z}),
\tag{W2}
\]
and \(\widehat V_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}\to_PV_{\Delta,z}\).  Hence the two-sided Wald interval has pointwise asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\).  If additionally \(\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},z}(P)\ge\delta_0>0\), its lower endpoint is at least \(\delta_0/2\) with probability tending to one.  These conclusions are pointwise; they are not uniform at an equality or rank-changing boundary.
statements.proof_tex:
Write the support of \(X\) as \(\{x_1,\ldots,x_D\}\).  The separate support coordinates in Definition \(\ref{def:gap-one-step}\) give
\[
 P(X=x_d)=E_P[U_d^X].
\tag{W3}
\]
For every retained cell, positivity of the support mass and retained-cell overlap make the following denominators nonzero:
\[
 p_{a,s}(x_d)
 =\frac{E_P[U^{(0)}_{d,a,s}]}{E_P[U_d^X]},
 \qquad
 m_{a,s,u}(x_d)
 =\frac{E_P[U^{(1,u)}_{d,a,s}]}{E_P[U^{(0)}_{d,a,s}]},
\tag{W4}
\]
and
\[
 E_P[\Delta Y_u\Delta Y_v\mid G=a,S=s,X=x_d]
 =\frac{E_P[U^{(2,u,v)}_{d,a,s}]}{E_P[U^{(0)}_{d,a,s}]}.
\tag{W5}
\]
Because \(D\), \(T\), and \(\mathcal G\) are finite, (W3)--(W5) reconstruct all support masses, cell probabilities, first moments, and second cross-moments.  The formulas in the core then reconstruct \(\pi\), \(q\), \(\theta\), \(\Psi\), \(\Omega\), \(Z^{\mathrm{OVS}}\), \(K_{\mathrm{OVS}}\), and \(r_{\mathrm{OVS}}\) as explicit functions of \(\mu(P)\).

The corrected score vector has mean zero.  Therefore the variance of the declared law-dependent comparator is
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_P\{b_z(P)'\Psi_P\}
 =b_z\{\mu(P)\}'\Omega\{\mu(P)\}b_z\{\mu(P)\}.
\tag{W6}
\]
Let \(b^{\mathrm{ref}}\) be the reference loading from Definition \(\ref{def:gap-one-step}\).  Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\) and finite-support conditioning give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 V_{\mathrm{OVS}}
 &=E_P[(\psi_P^0)^2]
 -E_P[r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)'K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)^\dagger
 r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)]\\
 &=b^{\mathrm{ref}\prime}\Omega\{\mu(P)\}b^{\mathrm{ref}}
 -\sum_{d=1}^D P(X=x_d)
 r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x_d)'K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x_d)^\dagger
 r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x_d).
 \end{aligned}
\tag{W7}
\]
Subtracting (W7) from (W6) is exactly formula (G4) defining \(F_z\).  This proves
\[
 F_z\{\mu(P)\}
 =\operatorname{Var}_P\{b_z(P)'\Psi_P\}-V_{\mathrm{OVS}}
 =\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},z}(P).
\tag{W8}
\]
In particular, the reconstruction differentiates the rule \(P\mapsto b_z(P)\); it does not incorrectly hold a numerical loading fixed while differentiating the law.

We next establish the stochastic order required by the selected-rank lemma.  The fourth-moment assumption and
\[
 |\Delta Y_u|^4\le 8(|Y_u|^4+|Y_{u-1}|^4),
 \qquad
 (\Delta Y_u\Delta Y_v)^2
 \le\frac12\{(\Delta Y_u)^4+(\Delta Y_v)^4\}
\tag{W9}
\]
show that every coordinate of \(U(O)\) has a finite second moment.  Coordinatewise Chebyshev inequalities, combined over the fixed dimension \(d_\mu\), yield
\[
 \widehat\mu-\mu(P)=O_P(n^{-1/2}),
 \qquad
 \Sigma_U:=\operatorname{Var}_P\{U(O)\}<\infty.
\tag{W10}
\]

At the fixed law, there are only finitely many matrices \(K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x_d)\) and comparator KKT matrices.  Each is real symmetric, and the minimum absolute value among all of their nonzero eigenvalues is strictly positive.  On the overlap domain their entries are continuously differentiable rational functions of \(\mu\); all ordinary denominators are nonzero by (W3)--(W5).  Lemma \(\ref{lem:fixed-support-selected-rank-delta}\), applied with \(z=\mu\), (W10), \(\tau_n\downarrow0\), and \(n^{-1/2}/\tau_n\to0\), therefore proves simultaneous population-rank recovery and
\[
 F_{z,\tau_n}(\widehat\mu)-F_z\{\mu(P)\}
 =d_z'\{\widehat\mu-\mu(P)\}+o_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{W11}
\]
Since \(\widehat\mu-\mu(P)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n[U(O_i)-\mu(P)]\), equations (W8) and (W11) give
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}-\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},z}(P)\}
 =\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_z(O_i)+o_P(1).
\tag{W12}
\]
The summands are independent and identically distributed by the sampling assumption, have mean zero by definition, and have variance \(V_{\Delta,z}\in(0,\infty)\) by (W10) and the stated positivity condition.  Lemma \(\ref{lem:iid-central-limit}\), followed by the elementary fact that adding an \(o_P(1)\) term preserves convergence at every continuity point, proves the normal limit in (W2).

It remains to prove variance consistency under the stated moments.  Rank recovery and continuity of the selected branch imply
\[
 \widehat d_z\longrightarrow_P d_z.
\tag{W13}
\]
For any entry \(W=U_jU_k\), \(E_P|W|<\infty\) by Cauchy--Schwarz and (W10).  Let \(W_M=W\mathbf 1\{|W|\le M\}\).  The sample average of bounded \(W_M\) converges in probability to its expectation by Chebyshev's inequality, while Markov's inequality gives, for every \(\epsilon>0\),
\[
 P\{\mathbb P_n|W-W_M|>\epsilon\}
 \le \epsilon^{-1}E_P[|W|\mathbf 1\{|W|>M\}].
\tag{W14}
\]
The right side tends to zero as \(M\to\infty\).  Finiteness of the matrix dimension and \(\widehat\mu\to_P\mu(P)\) consequently imply
\[
 \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
 \{U(O_i)-\widehat\mu\}\{U(O_i)-\widehat\mu\}'
 \longrightarrow_P\Sigma_U.
\tag{W15}
\]
Premultiplying and postmultiplying (W15) by \(\widehat d_z\), and using (W13), gives
\[
 \widehat V_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}
 \longrightarrow_P d_z'\Sigma_Ud_z=V_{\Delta,z}.
\tag{W16}
\]

Let \(z_{1-\alpha/2}\) be the \((1-\alpha/2)\)-quantile of the standard normal law.  Equations (W12) and (W16), with \(V_{\Delta,z}>0\), imply
\[
 T_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}\Rightarrow N(0,1),
\]
so the interval
\[
 \left[\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}
 -z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}/n},\ 
 \widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}
 +z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}/n}\right]
\]
has pointwise limiting coverage \(1-\alpha\).  Finally, (W12) gives \(\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}-\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},z}(P)=O_P(n^{-1/2})\), and (W16) makes the half-width \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\).  If \(\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},z}(P)\ge\delta_0>0\), their sum in absolute value is below \(\delta_0/2\) with probability tending to one.  The lower endpoint is then at least \(\delta_0/2\), as claimed.  The argument fixes the law and its selected ranks throughout, so it makes no uniform assertion at an equality or rank-changing boundary.
statements.justification: The explicit moment map closes pointwise inference for the published-bound gap in the certified finite-support regime.
statements.gap: The theorem is separated from equality and rank-changing boundaries and does not claim uniform coverage there.
statements.consumer: The backend may expose a gap estimate, plug-in standard error, and Wald interval when its fixed-support checks pass.

statements.statement:
In the two-period panel design with enabling cohort \(C\in\{2,\infty\}\), eligibility \(E\in\{0,1\}\), outcome change \(D=Y_2-Y_1\), and covariates \(X\), define \(p_{a,s}(x)=P(C=a,E=s\mid X=x)\), \(\mu_{a,s}(x)=E[D\mid C=a,E=s,X=x]\), and
\[
\tau(X)=D-\mu_{2,0}(X)-\mu_{\infty,1}(X)+\mu_{\infty,0}(X).
\]
Under the source's random-sampling, strong-overlap, no-anticipation, and conditional DDD parallel-trends assumptions, Ortiz--Villavicencio and Sant'Anna's Lemma A.2 states that the efficient influence function for \(\operatorname{ATT}(2,2)\) is
\[
\eta_{\mathrm{OVS}}
=w_{\mathrm{trt}}^{2,1}(C,E)\{\tau(X)-\operatorname{ATT}(2,2)\}
-w_{\mathrm{comp}}^{2,0}(C,E,X)\{D-\mu_{2,0}(X)\}
-w_{\mathrm{comp}}^{\infty,1}(C,E,X)\{D-\mu_{\infty,1}(X)\}
+w_{\mathrm{comp}}^{\infty,0}(C,E,X)\{D-\mu_{\infty,0}(X)\},
\]
where
\[
w_{\mathrm{trt}}^{2,1}(C,E)=\frac{\mathbf 1\{C=2,E=1\}}{E[\mathbf 1\{C=2,E=1\}]},
\qquad
w_{\mathrm{comp}}^{a,s}(C,E,X)
=\frac{\mathbf 1\{C=a,E=s\}p_{2,1}(X)/p_{a,s}(X)}{E[\mathbf 1\{C=a,E=s\}p_{2,1}(X)/p_{a,s}(X)]}.
\]

source.locator: Supplemental Appendix, Lemma A.2, PDF pages 44--45
source.verbatim_statement: Lemma A.2 (Efficient Influence Function). Suppose Assumptions S, SO, NA, and DDD-CPT hold. Let \(\tau(X)=Y_2-Y_1-m^{S=2,Q=0}_{Y_2-Y_1}(X)-m^{S=\infty,Q=1}_{Y_2-Y_1}(X)+m^{S=\infty,Q=0}_{Y_2-Y_1}(X)\). Then \(\eta_{\mathrm{eff}}=w^{S=2,Q=1}_{\mathrm{trt}}\{\tau(X)-\operatorname{ATT}(2,2)\}-w^{S=2,Q=0}_{\mathrm{comp}}\{Y_2-Y_1-m^{S=2,Q=0}_{Y_2-Y_1}(X)\}-w^{S=\infty,Q=1}_{\mathrm{comp}}\{Y_2-Y_1-m^{S=\infty,Q=1}_{Y_2-Y_1}(X)\}+w^{S=\infty,Q=0}_{\mathrm{comp}}\{Y_2-Y_1-m^{S=\infty,Q=0}_{Y_2-Y_1}(X)\}\) is the efficient influence function, where \(w^{S=2,Q=1}_{\mathrm{trt}}=\mathbf 1\{S=2,Q=1\}/E[\mathbf 1\{S=2,Q=1\}]\) and \(w^{S=g,Q=q}_{\mathrm{comp}}=\{\mathbf 1\{S=g,Q=q\}p^{S=2,Q=1}(X)/p^{S=g,Q=q}(X)\}/E[\mathbf 1\{S=g,Q=q\}p^{S=2,Q=1}(X)/p^{S=g,Q=q}(X)]\).

statements.statement:
In the two-period panel design of Akbari, Kiyavash, and Ghassami, let \(G_A,D_A\in\{0,1\}\), \(D_Y=Y_1-Y_0\), \(\mu_{a,s,\Delta}(X)=E[D_Y\mid X,G_A=a,D_A=s]\), \(\pi=E[G_AD_A]\),
\[
\psi_{\mathrm{pd}}
=E[\mu_{1,1,\Delta}(X)-\mu_{0,1,\Delta}(X)-\mu_{1,0,\Delta}(X)+\mu_{0,0,\Delta}(X)\mid G_A=1,D_A=1],
\]
\(\pi_{r,a,s}(X)=P(G_A=1,D_A=1\mid X)/P(G_A=a,D_A=s\mid X)\), and
\[
w_{a,s}(X,G_A,D_A)=G_AD_A-\mathbf 1\{G_A=a,D_A=s\}\pi_{r,a,s}(X).
\]
Their Theorem 5 states that, in the nonparametric model, the efficient influence function of the panel DDD target \(\psi_{\mathrm{pd}}\) is
\[
\psi_{\mathrm{pd}}^1(O)
=\frac1\pi\sum_{a,s\in\{0,1\}}(-1)^{a+s+1}
w_{a,s}(X,G_A,D_A)\{D_Y-\mu_{a,s,\Delta}(X)\}
-\frac{G_AD_A}{\pi}\psi_{\mathrm{pd}}.
\]

source.locator: Section 4.1 target definition and Theorem 5, equation (6), PDF pages 8--9
source.verbatim_statement: Section 4.1 defines \(\psi_{\mathrm{pd}}=E[(Y_1-Y_0-\mu_{0,1,\Delta}(X)-\mu_{1,0,\Delta}(X)+\mu_{0,0,\Delta}(X))\mathbf 1\{G=1,D=1\}]/E[\mathbf 1\{G=1,D=1\}]\). Theorem 5 states that its efficient influence function is \(\psi^1_{\mathrm{pd}}(O)=E[G D]^{-1}\sum_{g,d\in\{0,1\}}(-1)^{g+d+1}w_{g,d}(X,G,D)\{Y_1-Y_0-\mu_{g,d,\Delta}(X)\}-G D\psi_{\mathrm{pd}}/E[G D]\), where \(\mu_{g,d,\Delta}(X)=E[Y_1-Y_0\mid X,G=g,D=d]\), \(w_{g,d}=G D-\mathbf 1\{G=g,D=d\}\pi_{r,g,d}(X)\), and \(\pi_{r,g,d}(X)=p(G=1,D=1\mid X)/p(G=g,D=d\mid X)\).

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 3.2. Suppose that treatment adoption is staggered over time. Under Assumptions S, O, NA and PT-All, \(\operatorname{EIF}^{\operatorname{att}(g,t)}_{\mathrm{stg}}=\{\mathbf 1'\Omega_{gt}(X)^{-1}\}/\{\mathbf 1'\Omega_{gt}(X)^{-1}\mathbf 1\}\operatorname{IF}^{\operatorname{att}(g,t)}_{\mathrm{stg}}\) is the efficient influence function of \(\operatorname{ATT}(g,t)\).

statements.statement: Consider the two-period, two-cohort specialization with a single target \(k=(g,g)\), a single clean comparison \(\mathcal J_k=\{c\}\), the outcome change \(D=\Delta Y_g\), and unit aggregate weight \(\omega_k=1\). Relabel the target cohort and comparison cohort as \(G_A=1\) and \(G_A=0\), respectively, and relabel eligibility \(S\) as \(D_A\). Then the efficient influence functions in Ortiz--Villavicencio and Sant'Anna's Lemma A.2 and Akbari, Kiyavash, and Ghassami's Theorem 5 both reduce, term by term, to the core score \(\Psi_{k,c,P}\). Because the relevant published clean set is a singleton, there is no nonzero published OVS normal row and \[\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}=\psi_P^0=\Psi_{k,c,P}.\] For a scalar aggregate weight \(\omega_k\), all three expressions are multiplied by \(\omega_k\). At every fixed-finite-support conditional-mean-interior law covered by Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\), this common expression is the exhaustive staggered-DDD canonical gradient, so the two published panel-DDD formulas are exact just-identified special cases there. The algebraic reduction holds independently of that canonicality qualification and does not assert that the staggered-DiD conditional-efficiency model of Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie is nested in, or contains, the eligibility-gap DDD model.
statements.justification: The proposition gives the requested theorem-level comparison to the closest published panel-DDD efficient influence functions.
statements.gap: It proves a term-by-term exact special case, not a nesting relationship with the separate staggered-DiD conditional-efficiency model.
statements.consumer: The known-reductions theorem and backend score tests use this sourced equivalence.
